##
Nueva Living: New-Build Specialists on the Costa del Sol
We focus on new developments
Nueva Living was created for buyers who want straightforward help in the Costa del Sol new-build market.
About Nueva Living
## New builds are what we know
Nueva Living is a new-build real estate agency and buyer's agent. Because we only work with new and off-plan homes, we know the developers, the projects and the questions buyers should ask.
Our job is simple: show you what is available, explain what is good and help you leave the wrong options behind.
Founder
## Sasan Raftari
Founder, Nueva Living
Sasan founded Nueva Living to make the search for a new home on the Costa del Sol clearer and more focused.
Sasan has spent 17 years in sales, around ten of them in digital as a product manager, ecommerce manager and head of digital. He combines the two to build the Costa del Sol's most user-friendly and advanced portal for new-build property.
Contact him directly to discuss your search, ask about a project or build a shortlist around what matters to you.
Email sasan@nuevaliving.com Phone / WhatsApp +46 707 57 67 09
Co-Founder
## Sami Altun
Co-Founder, Nueva Living
Sami brings a background in business development and economics, with a practical focus on evaluating opportunities, structuring decisions and building long-term relationships.
At Nueva Living, he connects commercial insight with each buyer's priorities, helping keep project selection and the purchasing process clear, considered and grounded.
Email sami@nuevaliving.com Phone / WhatsApp +34 645 44 66 24

Direct conversations and project access across the main Costa del Sol areas.

100%
### Focused on New Builds
One clear focus keeps our advice useful and up to date.
On Every Project
## Everything we know, on the page
A brochure is written to make you enquire. A project page here is written so you need to enquire less.
### The availability list as the seller wrote it
Every home still for sale, with its floor, its built area and its price. Not a starting figure, but the actual range across the actual homes.
### Where each figure came from, and when
Every project names the document behind its numbers and the date they were confirmed. Where two documents disagree, we print both and say which said what.
### The gaps, left as gaps
If a seller has not issued a floorplan, the page says so rather than estimating. An empty cell is more useful than a number we invented.
### What we checked first
Whether the building licence is granted, whether your payments sit behind a bank guarantee, and whether the completion date is contractual or merely indicative.
### The trade-offs, in writing
Including the parts that cost you money. Where tax adds six figures to the asking price, that is on the page and not left for the notary to mention.
### Where it actually is
A routed map with real drive times to the beach, the airport and the town, rather than a marketing radius.
How We Are Paid
## The buyer pays us nothing
We are paid a commission by the developer when a purchase completes. You should know that before you take our advice, which is why it is on this page rather than buried in the small print.
Whether it changes what we show you is not something we can settle by claiming otherwise. Read a project page instead: the empty cells where a seller gave us no figure, the purchase costs added on top of the asking price, the two sources printed side by side when they disagree. That is the evidence, and it is the same on every development we publish.
The Company
## New company, experienced people
Nueva Living was founded in 2026. The company is new; the people running it are not, and the section above sets out what they did before this.
Nueva Living is a trading name of LIORA LIVING SL, NIF B88827472, Calle Las Torres, 3 (Aloha Gardens), 29660 Marbella, Malaga, Spain.
What Matters to Us
## Access, privacy and clear advice
### Privacy
We handle your requirements carefully and only share details when needed for your request.
### Fewer, Better Options
We focus on the projects worth considering rather than sending you a long catalogue.
### The Full Picture
Every recommendation includes the area, developer, timing and what may support future value.
FAQ
## Questions we are asked most
What does Nueva Living do?
We work only with new-build and off-plan homes on the Costa del Sol. We show what is available across the developments we cover, explain the trade-offs in writing and help you rule out the ones that do not fit.
What does it cost to use Nueva Living?
Nothing. We are paid a commission by the developer when a purchase completes. You should know that before you take our advice, which is why it is on this page rather than in the small print.
Is Nueva Living an estate agency?
We are an advisory for buyers of new developments rather than a general estate agency. Resale homes are not a market we work in.
Which areas do you cover?
Marbella, Nueva Andalucia, San Pedro de Alcantara, Benahavis, Estepona, Casares, and Mijas and Fuengirola.
Who runs Nueva Living?
Sasan Raftari, who founded the company, and Sami Altun, co-founder. Nueva Living is a trading name of LIORA LIVING SL, registered in Marbella, Spain.
Can I buy the same home directly from the developer?
Yes. What we add is the comparison: the availability list as the seller issued it, the purchase costs on top of the asking price, and the checks worth making before you reserve.
How do I know a project page is accurate?
Every project names the document its figures came from and the date they were confirmed. Where two documents disagree, both are printed. Where a seller has issued nothing, the page says so rather than estimating.

##
Off-Plan Buyer Advisory, Costa del Sol
Know what you are buying before you decide
We help you check the location, developer, finishes, payment plan and future resale appeal before you choose a home.
An Independent View
## Clear advice for the buyer
A developer brochure shows the project at its best. As a new-build real estate agency and buyer's agent, we help you look beyond it and understand what is genuinely strong, what is fairly standard and what needs a closer check.
How We Help
## The details we help you compare
### Compare Projects
We compare prices, orientation, amenities, completion dates and nearby alternatives side by side.
### Plan the Purchase
We talk through how you will use the home, rental plans, financing and what you may want later.
### Reserve with Clarity
We organise project documents, viewings, reservation details and an introduction to an independent lawyer.
Our Promise
## Straight answers, no pressure
### A Shorter, Better List
We would rather show you three suitable projects than thirty generic options.
### Real Urgency Only
We only flag urgency when availability, pricing or a reservation deadline genuinely changes.
FAQ
## Common buyer questions
Can foreigners buy property in Spain?
Yes. There are no restrictions on non-Spanish nationals buying property in Spain, whether as a resident or non-resident.
What is an NIE number and do I need one?
An NIE (Numero de Identificacion de Extranjero) is a tax ID number required for any property purchase in Spain by a non-Spanish national. Nueva Living can guide you through obtaining one before you reserve.
What costs should I budget for on top of the purchase price?
Buyers typically budget for transfer tax or VAT, notary fees, land registry fees and legal fees on top of the purchase price. Nueva Living provides a full, current cost breakdown for your chosen residence before you reserve.
Can I get a mortgage in Spain as a non-resident?
Many Spanish banks offer mortgages to non-resident buyers, typically financing a portion of the purchase price. Exact terms depend on the bank and your personal financial profile.
What is the difference between off-plan and completed properties?
Off-plan means the development is still under construction and is usually sold with staged payments through to completion. A completed property is ready to view and move into now.
How does the reservation and payment process work?
Reservation and payment structures vary by development and are set out in full before you reserve. Nueva Living reconfirms the current schedule for your chosen residence at every step.
Can I rent out the property after purchase?
This depends on the individual development and local regulations, which can vary by community and municipality. Nueva Living will confirm the specific rules for a development before you reserve.
Do I need a lawyer?
Yes, we strongly recommend independent legal representation for any property purchase in Spain. Nueva Living can put you in touch with independent lawyers experienced in Costa del Sol property.
The Mechanics
## How an off-plan purchase actually works
Three guides on the parts of the process buyers ask about most, each written against the statute or against the schedules our developers have supplied in writing.
### Bank Guarantees
What protects your deposit under Ley 38/1999, and the point before the building licence at which it does not yet apply.
### Payment Schedules
Reservation, contract, construction milestones and the balance at deed, using real figures from the projects on this site.
### Warranties and Snagging
The ten, three and one-year guarantees, who is liable under each, and why handover starts the clock.
Who We Are
## The people behind the advice
We work only with new and off-plan homes on the Costa del Sol, which is why we know the developers, the projects and the questions worth asking.

##
Costa del Sol Area Guide
Benahavís: where to buy above the coast
A low-density hillside market centred on privacy, golf, space and gated residential communities.
Living in Benahavís
## A quieter setting, still close to Marbella
Benahavís is not one single residential centre. La Quinta, Los Arqueros, Los Flamingos and the more secluded estates each offer a different balance of driving time, elevation, views and security. A car is essential in most communities.
The municipality is small and hilly, and much of it is protected countryside. That is why building is spread across a handful of separate communities rather than one continuous town, most of them between the village and the coast, in the stretch known as the Golden Triangle of golf.
Distances are short by car and not walkable. Puerto Banús is about fifteen minutes from the village and less from La Quinta and the lower communities, and Málaga airport is about an hour away. Most daily life here, from shopping to the beach, starts with a drive.
New-build supply is limited. Two developments are on our list at the moment, one of apartments and penthouses and one of duplex villas; their current prices and availability are in the project cards below, and we reconfirm both before any viewing.
01
### Best For
Buyers prioritising privacy, security, golf and larger indoor-outdoor spaces.
02
### Important Trade-off
Most homes require a car, and access times differ considerably between communities.
03
### Property Profile
Villas and elevated apartments often offer larger terraces, pools and open views.
04
### Location Choice
La Quinta is closer to Nueva Andalucía; higher and western communities feel more secluded.
Local Knowledge
## What makes Benahavís different
Small, hillside and quietly wealthy -- Benahavís works on its own terms.
01
### The dining capital claim
Benahavís has one of the highest restaurant-to-resident ratios on the coast, and locals genuinely mean it when they call it the area's culinary centre -- worth a lunch visit before you view anything.
02
### The village itself
Built into the hillside with views down the valley toward the coast, the old centre still feels like a mountain village rather than a Marbella suburb.
03
### The Río Verde gorge walk
A well-known hiking route following the river gorge down toward San Pedro -- one of the few genuine walking trails this close to major development.
04
### La Zagaleta and the gated hills
Some of the most private, security-gated communities on the Costa del Sol sit within Benahavís's boundaries, which shapes the area's reputation for discretion as much as its scenery does.
Where to Buy
## Not one place, but several
01
### La Quinta
The closest of the communities to Nueva Andalucía and to the coast, built around the golf. It is the shortest drive to Puerto Banús of the Benahavís addresses, which is the main reason buyers who want seclusion without isolation start here.
02
### The Golden Triangle
The stretch between Marbella, Benahavís village and Estepona, close to La Quinta golf and a short drive from Puerto Banús and the coast. Elevated plots here trade a few minutes of driving for open views.
03
### The village
The old core, set back in the hills and smaller in scale than anything around it. The current releases sit below in the golf communities rather than here, so buying in the village itself usually means an older house rather than a new one.
04
### The gated hills
La Zagaleta and the more secluded estates sit within the municipal boundaries and shape its reputation for discretion. Higher and more western communities feel more remote, and access times differ considerably between them.
05
### Los Arqueros
The community around the Los Arqueros golf club, on the hillside west of La Quinta. A golf-led address of villas and apartments, a little further from the coast than La Quinta.
06
### Los Flamingos
The estate around the Los Flamingos golf course, on the western side of the municipality towards Estepona. Plots tend to be larger, and the drive to the beach is longer.

## What buyers ask us about Benahavís
How much does property cost in Benahavís?
The average asking price for resale homes was €5,413 per m² in June 2026. Values vary considerably between communities and prime villas sit well above that, so the municipal average is a weaker guide here than in the denser coastal towns.
Which part of Benahavís should I look at?
Benahavís is not one residential centre. La Quinta, Los Arqueros, Los Flamingos and the more secluded estates each strike a different balance of driving time, elevation, views and security. La Quinta is closest to Nueva Andalucía; the higher and more western communities feel more secluded.
Do I need a car in Benahavís?
In most communities, yes. Access times differ considerably between them, and that difference is the main practical trade-off against the privacy, space and views the area is bought for.
What kind of property does Benahavís have?
Mostly villas and elevated apartments, typically with larger terraces, pools and open views than equivalent money buys on the coast itself. That is the trade the area offers: more space and more privacy, further from the sea.
Why is Benahavís known for its restaurants?
It has one of the highest restaurant-to-resident ratios on the coast, and locals genuinely mean it when they call it the area's culinary centre. It is worth a lunch visit before you view anything, because it tells you something about the place that a floorplan cannot.
Benahavís or Marbella?
Benahavís is a low-density hillside market built around privacy, golf, space and gated communities, and it asks slightly below Marbella's municipal average per m². Marbella gives you the town, the beaches and walkable daily life; Benahavís gives you seclusion and larger homes, and asks you to drive for both.
How far is Benahavís from the beach, Puerto Banús and the airport?
From the village, Puerto Banús is about fifteen minutes by car and Málaga airport about an hour. The lower communities, such as La Quinta, are closer to the coast, and the higher and more western estates are further. There is no walking to the sea, so the drive is part of the choice.
Which golf courses are there in Benahavís?
The best known are La Quinta, Los Arqueros and Los Flamingos, with La Zagaleta as a private club. Counts differ between sources, and the private clubs are open to members only.
Is Benahavís suited to living here all year, or only to holidays?
Both can work. The quiet and the security suit owners who are away part of the year. Full-time residents should test the daily drive, at school and commuting times, before choosing a community.
What new-build is available in Benahavís?
Supply is limited. Two developments are on our list: one of apartments and penthouses in the Golden Triangle and one of duplex villas. Current prices and availability are in the project cards on this page, and we reconfirm them before any viewing.

##
Costa del Sol Area Guide
Benalmádena: three centres, one coastline
A municipality of about 78,000 people between Torremolinos and Fuengirola, made of a hillside village, an inland town and a beach resort that are priced very differently.
Living in Benalmádena
## Three centres, three different prices
Benalmádena is not one town. Benalmádena Pueblo is a white village on the hillside above the coast, Arroyo de la Miel is the inland town where the shops, the cable car and the train station are, and Benalmádena Costa is the beach strip of hotels, apartment blocks and the marina. A few kilometres separate them, and the price per square metre separates them further.
The municipality covers a little over 27 km² between Torremolinos to the east and Fuengirola to the west, about 12 km from Málaga. It had 78,338 inhabitants in 2025, and the C1 commuter line stops at Arroyo de la Miel and Torremuelle with trains about every 20 minutes.
01
### Best For
Buyers who want a lived-in coastal municipality with a marina, long beaches and a commuter train to Málaga and its airport.
02
### Important Trade-off
The district decides the budget more than the municipality does, from €3,415 per m² in Arroyo de la Miel to €5,047 in Parque de la Paloma.
03
### Property Profile
Mostly apartments, from older blocks on the seafront to newer developments higher up the slope.
04
### Location Choice
The Costa for the sand and the marina, Arroyo de la Miel for the train and the shops, the Pueblo for the hillside village and its views.
Local Knowledge
## What makes Benalmádena different
A village, a marina, a cable car and a stupa, all inside one municipality of 27 km².
01
### The village on the hillside
Benalmádena Pueblo is the old village, white-walled and set on the hillside above the coast with views down to the water. At €3,742 per m² it asks less than the municipal average, and it is the part of Benalmádena that feels least like a resort.
02
### A cable car to Calamorro
A four-person cable car climbs from Arroyo de la Miel to the summit of Monte Calamorro, 769 metres above the sea, in a journey of about fifteen minutes. It is the quickest way to see how the three centres and the coast fit together.
03
### The largest stupa in Europe
The Benalmádena Stupa, built in 2003, is 33 metres tall and is the largest Buddhist stupa in Europe. It is one of the municipality’s best-known sights, and an unusual one on this coast.
04
### Puerto Marina
Puerto Marina is one of the larger marinas in Andalusia, with restaurants, shops and apartment blocks built around the harbour. Solymar - Puerto Marina averages €4,610 per m², above the municipal average.
Photography: Aapo Haapanen -- via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0).
Where to Buy
## Three centres and the edges between them
01
### Benalmádena Costa
The beach strip with the marina, the hotels and the apartment blocks. Parque de la Paloma averages €5,047 per m², Solymar - Puerto Marina €4,610, Torrequebrada €3,920 and Torremuelle €3,908, so even the front line is not one price.
02
### Arroyo de la Miel
The inland town between the Pueblo and the Costa, with the railway station, the shops and the start of the cable car. At €3,415 per m² it is the least expensive district.
03
### Benalmádena Pueblo
The old village on the hillside, at €3,742 per m². Narrow streets, squares and views of the coast, set back from the sand.
04
### El Higuerón - Capellanía
The district at the Fuengirola end of the municipality, at €4,892 per m², the second highest of the districts. Part of El Higuerón lies across the boundary in Fuengirola.

## What buyers ask us about Benalmádena
How much does property cost in Benalmádena?
The average asking price for resale homes was €4,188 per m² in September 2026, up 5.1% on a year earlier. Idealista changed its method in July 2026, so compare it with the June figures on the other area pages as an approximation. Inside the municipality the range runs from €3,415 in Arroyo de la Miel to €5,047 in Parque de la Paloma.
Which part of Benalmádena should I look at?
It depends on what you want to be near. Benalmádena Costa and El Higuerón ask the most and put you closest to the sand and the marina. Arroyo de la Miel asks the least and is where the train, the shops and the cable car are. The Pueblo sits between them on price, on the hillside, with views and a village feel.
How far is Benalmádena from Málaga airport?
About 19 kilometres by road. The C1 commuter line runs through Arroyo de la Miel and Torremuelle to the airport and Málaga with trains about every 20 minutes, so the airport does not depend on a car.
Can you walk to the beach from Benalmádena?
From Benalmádena Costa, yes: the municipality has almost ten kilometres of beach. From Arroyo de la Miel it is a short drive, and from the Pueblo the coast is further down the hill, so a car or a taxi is the realistic way.
Benalmádena or Torremolinos?
They share a boundary and a train line, and their averages are almost the same: €4,188 per m² in Benalmádena and €4,199 in Torremolinos in September 2026. Torremolinos is a denser town along nearly eight kilometres of beach, with older layers of tourism; Benalmádena has a marina, a hillside village and three distinct centres.
Is Benalmádena lived in all year?
Yes. About 78,000 people live in the municipality, and Arroyo de la Miel and the Pueblo work as ordinary residential towns outside the summer. The Costa is the busiest part in season.

##
Costa del Sol Area Guide
Casares, area by area: where to buy and what it costs
The last municipality before the Cadiz border, and three separate markets in one: a hilltop white village, an inland golf valley and a low-rise stretch of coast.
Living in Casares
## Three Casares, and they barely resemble each other
Casares pueblo is the hilltop white village most people picture: steep, historic and genuinely lived in, but a real drive from the beach. The coastal strip -- Marina de Casares, Bahía de Casares and Casares Costa -- is low-rise, quiet and walkable to the sand. Between the two sits a golf valley built around Casares Golf, Doña Julia and Finca Cortesín.
Buyers usually arrive here after looking at Estepona and finding the same specification for less. The trade-off is that Casares is a car-dependent municipality with fewer everyday services than a town, and the three zones are far enough apart that choosing between them matters more than choosing a building.
01
### Best For
Buyers who want new-build near the coast at below Estepona pricing, and are comfortable driving for services.
02
### Important Trade-off
The pueblo, the golf valley and the coast are separate markets. Daily life differs sharply between them.
03
### Property Profile
Mostly low-rise apartments and townhouses on the coast and around the golf courses; village houses in the pueblo.
04
### Location Choice
Marina de Casares is the most walkable; Doña Julia the most affordable; the pueblo the most characterful and least convenient.
Local Knowledge
## What makes Casares different
Less built-out than its neighbours, and priced accordingly -- but the geography does most of the work here.
01
### A championship course, quietly
Finca Cortesín hosted the Solheim Cup in September 2023. It sits roughly six minutes from the new-build releases on this stretch, which is unusual proximity to a course of that standing without Sotogrande or Marbella pricing.
02
### The village is not the market
Casares pueblo is what the municipality is known for, but very little new-build happens there. Almost all current supply is on the coastal strip and around the golf courses, several kilometres and a winding road away.
03
### Estepona does the heavy lifting
Casares has limited everyday services of its own. Estepona is under 15 minutes away and is where most residents shop, eat out and see a doctor -- worth driving the route at least once before committing.
04
### Two airports, not one
Málaga is under an hour. Gibraltar is closer still, which matters more to UK buyers than the Malaga-centric marketing on this coast usually admits.

Where to Buy
## Three markets, and they barely overlap
01
### The coastal strip
Marina de Casares, Bahía de Casares and Casares Costa: low-rise, quiet and walkable to the sand. Marina de Casares is the most walkable of the three and asks the highest price per m² in the municipality, at €4,455.
02
### The golf valley
Casares Golf, Doña Julia and Finca Cortesín. Doña Julia is the most affordable address in the municipality at €3,905 per m², and Finca Cortesín — which hosted the Solheim Cup in September 2023 — sits roughly six minutes from the current releases on this stretch.
03
### Casares pueblo
The hilltop white village the municipality is known for: steep, historic and genuinely lived in, but a real drive from the beach. It asks €4,447 per m², close to the coastal average, and sees very little new construction.
04
### The hillside behind
Elevated plots against the Sierra Bermeja Nature Park, under fifteen minutes from Estepona and about thirty from Marbella. This is where the current new-build release sits.

## What buyers ask us about Casares
How much does property cost in Casares?
The municipal average asking price for resale homes was €4,242 per m² in August 2026, but that average hides more than it shows. Marina de Casares asks €4,455, Casares pueblo €4,447, Casares Golf and Casares del Sol €4,228, Bahía de Casares €4,121 and Doña Julia Golf €3,905. Is Casares cheaper than Estepona?
Generally, yes — but the figures on this page are not a like-for-like comparison. The Casares averages come from Fotocasa, because the Idealista municipal report does not break Casares down by zone, while the Estepona figure comes from Idealista. Which part of Casares should I buy in?
The hilltop pueblo, the golf valley and the coastal strip are three separate markets and daily life differs sharply between them. Marina de Casares is the most walkable, Doña Julia the most affordable, and the pueblo the most characterful and the least convenient.
Where do people in Casares do their everyday shopping?
Mostly in Estepona, which is under fifteen minutes away. Casares has limited everyday services of its own, so it is worth driving that route at least once before committing rather than reading it off a map.
Which airport is closest to Casares?
Málaga is under an hour by car, and Gibraltar is closer still. That second option matters more to UK buyers than the Malaga-centric marketing on this coast usually admits, and it is worth factoring into how often you realistically expect to travel.
What kind of new-build is available in Casares?

##
Costa del Sol Area Guide
Estepona, area by area: where to buy and what it costs
A walkable town, long seafront and strong new-build supply, with a calmer pace than central Marbella.
Living in Estepona
## Coastal living with room to breathe
The main choice is between the walkable town centre, beachside communities and the New Golden Mile. The latter offers newer residential projects between Estepona and Marbella, but daily life is generally more car-dependent.
01
### Best For
Buyers seeking a practical coastal base with more value range than central Marbella.
02
### Town or New Golden Mile
The centre offers walkability; newer coastal communities offer pools, space and managed grounds.
03
### Daily Life
The old town, promenade, schools, healthcare and shops remain active throughout the year.
04
### Access
The A-7 connects Estepona with Marbella, Gibraltar and Málaga Airport; journey times vary with traffic.
Local Knowledge
## What makes Estepona different
Estepona has changed more than any other town on this coast in the last decade -- worth understanding before you compare it to Marbella.
01
### Calle Real and the flower streets
A years-long municipal push to repaint facades and hang flower pots on every balcony earned Estepona the nickname “Garden of the Costa del Sol.” It is one of the few old towns here that feels cared for rather than preserved for tourists.
02
### The Orchidarium
A striking glass botanical garden in the town centre, home to thousands of orchid species -- an unusual cultural anchor for a coastal town this size.
03
### The port and fish market
Still a working fishing harbour, not just a marina. The daily catch shows up on the same evening's restaurant menus along the front.
04
### The New Golden Mile
The stretch running east from Estepona toward Marbella, including Cancelada, is where most of the town's new-development activity sits -- close to the coast without central Marbella's density or prices.
Where to Buy
## Five settings, priced differently
01
### The town and its edges
Estepona's own centre, with the old town, the promenade, schools, healthcare and shops active through the year. Las Mesas sits on the eastern edge between the sea and the Sierra Bermeja; Bahía Dorada is on the western edge, around a ten-minute walk from Arroyo Vaquero beach.
02
### The New Golden Mile
The coastal stretch between Estepona and San Pedro Alcántara, and where most of the newer residential projects are. Cancelada, Bel Air and La Resina all sit on it, with direct access to the coast road and Marbella and Estepona both within reach.
03
### New developments in Cancelada
A quiet residential area on the New Golden Mile between Estepona and Marbella, with direct access to the coast road and the beach close by. Estepona and Puerto Banús are each 12 km away and Marbella 21 km. The new developments here range from low-rise apartments and penthouses to two- and three-bedroom ground-floor homes with a garden or large terraces.
04
### El Campanario and the golf urbanisations
An established golf urbanisation on the New Golden Mile with the clubhouse inside it and the coast a short drive south. Suits buyers who want managed grounds and a course on the doorstep rather than a town centre.
05
### The beachside
Guadalobon sits between the Mediterranean and the Sierra Bermeja, close to the beach and Valle Romano Golf, with Marbella around twenty to twenty-five minutes away. Beachside pricing runs above the municipal average.

## What buyers ask us about Estepona
How much does property cost in Estepona?
The average asking price for resale homes was €4,329 per m² in June 2026, against €5,608 for Marbella on the same measure and month. Beachside and newly built homes are generally priced above the local average rather than at it, so treat the figure as a starting point for the municipality, not a guide to any one address.
Should I buy in Estepona town or on the New Golden Mile?
The town centre gives you walkability: the old town, the promenade, schools, healthcare and shops stay active through the year. The New Golden Mile, between Estepona and Marbella, is where the newer residential projects are, with pools, space and managed grounds, but daily life there is generally more car-dependent.
How do you get to Málaga airport from Estepona?
By car, on the A-7, which connects Estepona with Marbella, Gibraltar and the airport. Journey times vary considerably with traffic and with where in the municipality you are, so the drive is worth timing from the specific address rather than from the town centre.
Is Estepona quieter than Marbella?
Generally yes. It has a calmer pace than central Marbella while keeping a working town behind it rather than a resort strip, which is what makes it practical outside the season as well as during it.
Is there much new-build in Estepona?
Estepona has one of the stronger new-build pipelines on this coast, spread between the town, the beachside communities and the New Golden Mile. The developments we currently hold information on are listed above, with real availability rather than a general search.
Estepona or Casares — which should I look at?
Casares sits immediately west and is where buyers often look for new-build near the coast at lower pricing, but it has limited everyday services of its own and Estepona is where most Casares residents shop, eat out and see a doctor. If you want the services on your doorstep rather than fifteen minutes away, that argues for Estepona.
Which parts of Estepona have new-build homes?
New-build in Estepona is spread across several settings: the town and its edges, including Las Mesas and Bahía Dorada; the New Golden Mile towards Marbella, with Cancelada, Bel Air and La Resina; the golf urbanisations around El Campanario; and the beachside at Guadalobon. Prices differ between them, and beachside homes generally sit above the municipal average, so compare projects within one setting before comparing prices across settings.
Is Cancelada a good area for a new-build?
Cancelada is a quiet residential area on the New Golden Mile between Estepona and Marbella, with direct access to the coast road and the beach close by. Estepona and Puerto Banús are each 12 km away and Marbella 21 km. The new developments here range from low-rise apartments and penthouses to ground-floor homes with a garden or large terraces. It suits buyers who want a calmer base than a town centre and accept that daily errands are by car.

## A place that works beyond the summer
Marbella works for both full-time living and longer stays, but the micro-location matters. Marbella East is quieter and more residential, the Golden Mile prioritises access to the centre and Puerto Banús, and the hills trade walkability for privacy and views.

## What makes Marbella Marbella
Beyond the property listings, this is the texture of daily life that keeps people coming back.
01
### Casco Antiguo
The old town's Plaza de los Naranjos, ringed by orange trees, is still the best place to feel Marbella before the marina culture took over -- narrow whitewashed lanes, tapas bars and a genuinely local pace.
02
### Puerto Banús
The marina is the coast's best-known stage: superyachts, boutique shopping and a see-and-be-seen restaurant scene. It also anchors property values across Nueva Andalucía and the western Golden Mile.
03
### The Golden Mile
The palm-lined stretch between central Marbella and Puerto Banús, home to Puente Románo and the Marbella Club -- still the reference point for prime beachside real estate on this coast.
04
### La Concha
The limestone peak behind the town gives Marbella its skyline and a genuinely good hiking trail, with views back over the coast that most visitors never see.

Where to Buy
## Where the current releases actually sit
01
### Marbella East
Elviria and Rio Real. Elviria West is a growing part of eastern Marbella close to golf courses, beach clubs and Elviria's own shops and restaurants; Rio Real is an established neighbourhood close to the beach, golf and the town centre. Quieter and more residential than the centre, and where most of our current Marbella stock sits.
02
### The Golden Mile
The palm-lined stretch between central Marbella and Puerto Banús, home to Puente Romano and the Marbella Club and still the reference point for prime beachside property on this coast. Expect pricing above the municipal average rather than at it.
03
### Marbella West
San Pedro Alcántara is walkable and established, close to the beach with easy access to Puerto Banús and the A-7. Guadalmina sits between San Pedro and Puerto Banús, surrounded by golf. Cortijo Blanco is level and a few streets back from the sand, with the promenade, San Pedro centre and Puerto Banús all within walking distance.
04
### The hills behind the coast
Elevated positions that trade walkability for privacy, space and open views. A car is assumed rather than optional, and access times differ enough between communities that the drive is worth timing from the specific address.

## What buyers ask us about Marbella
How much does property cost in Marbella?
The average asking price for resale homes across the municipality was €5,608 per m² in June 2026. That figure spans very different markets: beachside Golden Mile addresses, the residential east and the hillside communities do not trade at the same level, and new developments generally sit above the resale average rather than at it.
Which part of Marbella should I buy in?
It depends on how you intend to use the home. Marbella East is quieter and more residential, the Golden Mile prioritises access to the centre and Puerto Banús, and the hills trade walkability for privacy and views. Beachside, town, golf and hillside homes give genuinely different daily routines within the same municipality.
How far is Marbella from Málaga airport?
Central Marbella is typically around 40 to 45 minutes by car. Addresses further east shorten that and the hillside communities lengthen it, so it is worth checking the drive from the specific address rather than from the town.
Does Marbella work for year-round living, or only in summer?
It works year-round, which is what separates it from much of the coast. International schools, private healthcare, shopping and restaurants stay open and staffed outside the season, which is what makes longer stays and full-time living practical here.
Is new-build supply in Marbella limited?
Land close to the sea is largely built out, so most current new-build activity sits in the eastern side of the municipality and the hillside communities rather than on the Golden Mile itself. The developments we currently hold information on are listed above, with real availability rather than a general search.
Marbella or Nueva Andalucía — what is the difference?
Nueva Andalucía is a residential area within the same municipality, built around golf and close to Puerto Banús, and it asks a higher average price per m² than Marbella as a whole. Two distinct coastal markets offering beaches, established services and easier access towards Málaga.
Living in Mijas & Fuengirola
## More choice, easy access and daily convenience
Fuengirola is urban, walkable and rail-connected. Mijas ranges from the village and La Cala to golf and hillside communities, where a car is usually needed. The right choice depends more on the exact setting than the municipality name.
01
### Best For
Buyers prioritising everyday convenience, transport links and a broader price range.

Best suited to buyers wanting a walkable town, long seafront and rail access to Málaga Airport.
03
### Mijas
La Cala, Mijas Pueblo and the inland golf communities offer very different lifestyles and access.
04
### Property Choice
Urban apartments, coastal townhouses and hillside villas cover a wider range of needs.
Local Knowledge
## What makes Mijas & Fuengirola different
The most functional stretch of this coast, and increasingly one of the most interesting.
01
### Mijas Pueblo
A whitewashed hillside village above Fuengirola with donkey taxis, viewpoints back over the coast and a genuinely old-Andalusia feel that the beach towns below it don't have.
02
### The Cercanías train line
A direct commuter rail connection to Málaga and the airport -- a practical advantage this stretch of coast has that Marbella and Estepona don't.
03
### Fuengirola's paseo marítimo and Bioparc
A long beachfront promenade and a well-regarded zoo built around natural habitats, both genuinely used by residents rather than just visitors.
04
### Castillo Sohail
A restored 10th-century fortress at the mouth of the Río Fuengirola, now used as a summer concert venue -- one of the coast's more distinctive landmarks.
Where to Buy
## Four settings, one price range apart
01
### Las Lagunas
The most active district of Mijas, between Fuengirola and Mijas Pueblo, with the Parque Comercial Miramar shopping and leisure centre directly alongside it. The most urban and the most everyday-practical of the settings here.
02
### Mijas Pueblo and the hills
A whitewashed hillside village above Fuengirola with viewpoints back over the coast and a genuinely old-Andalusia feel the beach towns below do not have. Hilltop plots nearby sit next to Cerrado del Águila golf, within reach of La Cala, Fuengirola and Marbella.
03
### Fuengirola
Urban, walkable and rail-connected, with a long beachfront promenade and services used by residents rather than only visitors. It asks €4,483 per m² against €3,773 in Mijas, and it is the address to look at if the train matters.
04
### Torremuelle and the Benalmádena edge
On the coast at Benalmádena, a short walk from the beach through a landscaped public park. It sits on the airport side of this stretch, which shortens the transfer further again.

## What buyers ask us about Mijas & Fuengirola
How much does property cost in Mijas and Fuengirola?
The average asking price for resale homes in June 2026 was €3,773 per m² in Mijas and €4,483 in Fuengirola. Both sit below Marbella's €5,608 on the same measure and month, which is the clearest reason buyers look at this stretch.
Mijas or Fuengirola — what is the difference?
Fuengirola is urban, walkable and rail-connected. Mijas ranges from the hillside village and La Cala to the inland golf communities, where a car is usually needed. The right choice depends far more on the exact setting than on which municipality the address falls in.
Can you reach Málaga airport by train from here?
Yes. The Cercanías commuter line runs directly to Málaga and the airport — a practical advantage this stretch of coast has that Marbella and Estepona do not. It is the main reason buyers who expect frequent short trips end up looking here.
Is this stretch cheaper than Marbella?
Yes, and measurably so: both municipal averages sit below Marbella's on the same Idealista measure for the same month. What you trade is prestige rather than access — the airport is closer from here than it is from Marbella.
Does it work outside the summer season?
It is the most functional stretch of this coast for year-round living, precisely because it is not built primarily around visitors. Fuengirola's promenade, shops and services are used by residents rather than only by tourists, and the rail line runs all year.
What kind of property is available?
A wider range than most of the coast: urban apartments in Fuengirola, coastal townhouses, and hillside and golf villas in Mijas. That range is the other half of why the price averages sit where they do.

##
Costa del Sol Area Guide
San Pedro de Alcántara: a real town beside Puerto Banús
A working Andalusian town inside the municipality of Marbella, with a street grid, a beach and a boulevard, priced below the resort addresses on either side.
Living in San Pedro de Alcántara
## A town that works when the visitors leave
San Pedro was a town before the coast became a resort. It began in 1860 as an agricultural colony, which is why the centre is a grid of ordinary streets around a church square, with a market, schools and a health centre rather than a parade of restaurants. People live here through the winter.
It runs from the Guadalmina river in the west, where Estepona and Benahavís begin, to the Guadaiza in the east, where Nueva Andalucía begins. Between those two rivers the price moves far more than the distance does.
01
### Best For
Buyers who want a town to live in year-round, a few minutes from Puerto Banús.
02
### The Boulevard
The old coast road runs in a tunnel under the town, and the surface above it is a park.
03
### Two Halves
Guadalmina and the beachside strip price like Marbella. The pueblo does not.
04
### Check the Side of the Road
The A-7 still separates the beachside communities from the town centre.
Local Knowledge
## What makes San Pedro different
Most of what sets San Pedro apart was here before the coast was developed.
01
### The boulevard over the bypass
The old N-340 was buried through the town and the surface handed back as a park of about 11,000 m²: fountains, a cycle lane, five playgrounds and an amphitheatre seating 500. It opened in 2014, and it is why the centre is as quiet as it is.
02
### Roman and early-Christian ruins
The baths at Las Bóvedas date from the second century and the basilica at Vega del Mar from the late fourth, both near the mouth of the Guadalmina. Little else on this stretch of coast is still standing from that far back.
03
### Guadalmina golf
The course opened in 1959, the first in Marbella and six years ahead of Río Real. The residential grid that grew around it is the most expensive part of San Pedro after the beachside strip.
04
### A colony rather than a resort
The agricultural colony of 1860 gave the town its grid, its street names and its industrial remains. It is why the centre reads as a Spanish town and not as a development.
Photography: Dcarolina.2000 -- via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0).
Where to Buy
## One town, four different prices
01
### Linda Vista, Nueva Alcántara and Cortijo Blanco
The beachside strip between the A-7 and the sea, and the most expensive part of San Pedro at €5,644 per m² in August 2026. Two of the projects on this page sit here.
02
### Guadalmina Baja
West of the town towards the Guadalmina river, between the road and the sea. Established, low-density and just above the San Pedro average at €5,158 per m².
03
### Guadalmina Alta
The golf side of the river, inland of the A-7, at €4,290 per m². It rose faster than anywhere else in the town over the year to August 2026.
04
### San Pedro pueblo
The original grid: the church square, the market, the schools and the boulevard. At €3,722 per m² it is the cheapest part of San Pedro and the part that most resembles a town.

## What buyers ask us about San Pedro de Alcántara
How much does property cost in San Pedro de Alcántara?
The average asking price for resale homes was €4,600 per m² in August 2026, below the Marbella municipal average of €5,608 and well below neighbouring Nueva Andalucía at €6,048. The spread inside the town is wide: the pueblo averaged €3,722 while Linda Vista, Nueva Alcántara and Cortijo Blanco averaged €5,644.
Is San Pedro part of Marbella?
Yes. It is a district of the municipality of Marbella, roughly ten kilometres west of the town centre, with its own centre, services and identity rather than the character of a suburb.
What is the boulevard in San Pedro?
The old N-340 coast road was put in a tunnel under the town and the surface above it turned into a park, opened in 2014. It carries about 11,000 m² of green space, fountains, a cycle lane, five playgrounds and an amphitheatre for 500 people, and it is the main reason the centre is quiet.
San Pedro or Nueva Andalucía?
They meet at the Guadaiza river and they are not the same proposition. Nueva Andalucía is built around golf and second homes and averages €6,048 per m². San Pedro is a working town with a school run and a weekly market, and averages €4,600. Puerto Banús is minutes from both.
Which part of San Pedro should I look at?
It depends on what you are paying for. Guadalmina Baja and the beachside strip between the A-7 and the sea carry the highest prices and the shortest walk to the sand. Guadalmina Alta and the pueblo cost materially less and give you the town instead. Which side of the A-7 you end up on changes daily life more than the price gap suggests.
Can you walk to the beach from San Pedro?
From the beachside communities, yes. From the town centre it is a few minutes by car or bicycle, with the A-7 in between. The seafront promenade runs along the beach itself and continues west towards Guadalmina.

##
Costa del Sol Area Guide
Torremolinos: the first resort on the coast
A compact town 13 km from Málaga, with nearly eight kilometres of beach, a train to the airport and prices that rose 7.1% in the year to September 2026.
Living in Torremolinos
## The oldest resort on the coast, and a town in its own right
Torremolinos was the first resort on the Costa del Sol. The Hotel Pez Espada opened in 1959 as the coast’s first luxury hotel, and by 1965 the town was an established destination. Before that it was a small settlement whose watchtower, the Torre Pimentel, dates from the 14th century.
Today it is a town of about 71,000 people, 13 km from Málaga and about ten minutes from the airport by train, with five Cercanías stations. It covers around 20 km², and its beach runs for nearly eight kilometres along the western shore of the Bay of Málaga.
01
### Best For
Buyers who want a walkable resort town with a long beach, year-round services and the airport minutes away by train.
02
### Important Trade-off
The district sets the price more than the town does, from €2,704 per m² in El Pinar - Palacio de Congresos to €5,222 in Playamar.
03
### Property Profile
Mostly apartments, from older blocks near the seafront to newer buildings further back.
04
### Location Choice
Playamar and El Bajondillo for the sand, La Carihuela for the older seafront district, the centre for the shops and the station.
Local Knowledge
## What makes Torremolinos different
A town that was already a resort before most of the coast had one.
01
### The first resort
The Hotel Pez Espada opened in 1959 as the coast’s first luxury hotel, and by 1965 Torremolinos was an established destination. It has had longer than any other town on the Costa del Sol to become a place people live in as well as visit.
02
### The watchtowers
The Torre Pimentel dates from the 14th century and appears in the ordinances of 1497 as the Torre de los Molinos. The Castillo de Santa Clara dates from 1763.
03
### An early golf course
A golf course opened here in 1928, described as the oldest golf club on the Spanish mainland.
04
### Nearly eight kilometres of beach
The beach runs for nearly eight kilometres along the western shore of the Bay of Málaga. The town received more than a million visitors and five million bed stays in 2023, so the seafront is busy in season.

03
### The centre and Montemar
The centre averages €3,840 and Montemar €3,933, both a little below the town average, with the shops and services of the town around them.
04
### El Pinar, El Pinillo and La Leala
El Pinar - Palacio de Congresos is the least expensive district at €2,704 per m². El Pinillo averages €3,702 and La Leala - El Saltillo €3,735.

##
Real Estate Agency, Developer or Buyer's Agent · Costa del Sol 2026
Agency, developer or buyer's agent: who to buy through
There are three ways to buy a new-build on the Costa del Sol. They differ less in price than most buyers expect, and more in whose side the person answering your questions is on.
Written by Sasan Raftari · Updated 24 November 2026
Nueva Living is one of the three options: a new-build real estate agency and buyer's agent. Read this knowing that. We have set out the trade-offs the way we would explain them to a friend, including where buying another way makes more sense.
Compare the Three Routes
Speak With an Advisor
Three Routes
## The same home, three ways in
## A general real estate agency
Who you deal with
An agent who sells both resale and new-build homes, from the agency's own listings and from the developments it has an agreement with.
Who pays
On a new-build the developer pays the agency's commission, and on a resale it is usually the seller. Either way it is part of the price rather than a bill sent to you.
Choice
As wide as the agency's agreements. Many agencies on the coast are strongest in resale and show a handful of new developments alongside it.
Best for
Buyers still deciding between resale and new-build, who want one agent to show them both.
Watch for
The agent is paid from the seller's side of the sale. Ask which developments the agency does not work with, and why.
## Direct from the developer
Who you deal with
The developer's own sales office or show flat.
Who pays
No agent is involved, but the price is usually the same. Most developers on the coast publish one price list for everyone and pay agents from their own marketing budget, so coming direct rarely makes the home cheaper.
Choice
That developer's projects only.
Best for
Buyers who have already chosen the development and want the people who know the building best, sometimes with first pick of the units at launch.
Watch for
A sales office sells its own project. Nobody in the room compares it with the development across the road.
## A new-build specialist or buyer's agent
Who you deal with
An agency that works only with new developments and takes the buyer's side of the search: shortlisting, comparing and checking projects across many developers.
Who pays
With us, the developer pays the commission when the purchase completes and the buyer pays nothing. Some buyer's agents charge the buyer a fee instead, or as well, so ask before the search starts.
Choice
Across developers and areas. We publish 130 current developments from Torremolinos to Casares, from €213,000 to €11.5 million.
Best for
Buyers who know they want a new-build and want the projects compared side by side, with prices, payment schedules and delivery dates on the same page.
Watch for
The agent is still paid on completion, and only by the developers it works with. Ask how it is paid and which developers it does not cover.
## What it costs you
On a new-build you pay the developer's list price whichever route you take. What changes the total is tax and fees: in Andalucía a new-build carries IVA at 10% and AJD at 1.2%, plus notary, registry and legal fees, and none of that depends on who introduced you. See what a new-build actually costs in Andalucia for the figures.
The real difference between the three routes is not the price. It is how many projects you see before you choose, and whether anyone compares them for you.
Whoever You Buy Through
## Four things to check
### The bank guarantee
Under Spanish law, money paid before completion must be covered by a bank guarantee or insurance policy in your name. Of the 130 developments we publish, 114 are off-plan or under construction, so this applies to most new-build purchases on the coast. Ask for it with the contract, not after.
### The building licence
Confirm the building licence has been granted. The statutory guarantee over your payments only begins once it has, and a project can be marketed before that point.
### The price list
Ask for the developer's dated price list and what each price includes: parking, storage, furniture, VAT. A price that exists only in a message is not a price.
### The agent's company
Andalucía created a register of estate agents in 2025, but it is not open yet and registering is not required to practise. So check the company behind the agent: its legal name and tax number (CIF), its entry in the Registro Mercantil, and, in writing, who pays it.
Whoever you buy through, use your own independent lawyer to check the contract, the licence and the guarantee before you pay more than the reservation. See how the bank guarantee works .
Common Questions
## What buyers ask before choosing
Is it cheaper to buy a new-build directly from the developer?
Usually not. Most developers on the Costa del Sol publish one price list and pay the agent's commission from their own budget, so coming direct rarely lowers the price. If a developer does offer a lower price for a direct purchase, get it in writing on the dated price list.
Who pays the estate agent's commission in Spain?
On a new-build the developer pays it, and on a resale usually the seller. The buyer pays the agent nothing in either case, unless they have hired a buyer's agent on a fee, which should be agreed in writing before the search starts.
What does a buyer's agent do in Spain?
A buyer's agent works on the buyer's side of the search: finding, comparing and checking homes rather than selling one particular listing. On the Costa del Sol most are paid by the developer or the seller when the purchase completes, and some charge the buyer a fee.
Can I use more than one agent?
Yes, but a developer pays one commission per sale, normally to whoever introduced you to that development first. Tell each agent which developments you have already seen or been introduced to, so there is no dispute later.
Do I still need a lawyer if I use an agent?
Yes. An agent, a developer and a lawyer do different jobs. Your own independent lawyer checks the contract, the licence and the bank guarantee, and an agent's advice does not replace that.
Once you have chosen, the next step is the purchase itself. See how buying a new-build works , step by step.

pages.text:
##
Bank Guarantees on Off-Plan Property · 2026 Guide
What actually protects your deposit
Spanish law guarantees the money you pay during construction. It does not guarantee all of it, from the moment you pay it, and the gap is where buyers get caught.
Written by Sasan Raftari · Updated 24 August 2026
When you buy off-plan you pay for a home that does not exist yet. Spanish law answers that with a specific mechanism: the money you hand over during construction has to be guaranteed, held apart from the developer's own funds, and returned with interest if the home is never delivered. Knowing exactly how that protection works -- and the one point at which it does not yet apply -- is the difference between an informed off-plan purchase and a hopeful one.
The Pre-Licence Gap
Ask About a Specific Project
The Law As It Stands
## Ley 38/1999, not Ley 57/1968
A great deal of English-language material about Spanish off-plan purchases still cites Ley 57/1968 as the source of your protection. That law was repealed with effect from 1 January 2016. Its regime was carried over, with changes, into the first additional provision of Ley 38/1999 (the Ley de Ordenación de la Edificación), in the wording given to it by Ley 20/2015. If a page tells you Ley 57/1968 protects your deposit today, it has not been updated in a decade -- and the changes are not cosmetic.
What The Developer Must Do
## Four obligations, not one
A segregated account
Advance payments must be received through a credit institution and deposited in a special account, kept separate from any other class of funds. Money may only leave that account for costs arising directly from the construction of those homes. It is not the developer's working capital.
A guarantee
Repayment must be guaranteed, either by a seguro de caución with an insurer authorised to operate in Spain, or by an aval solidario issued by an authorised credit institution. Both are acceptable; what matters is that one of them exists and names you.
Disclosure in the contract
The purchase contract itself must state the developer's obligation to repay, identify the insurer or guarantor, and identify the credit institution and the account. At signing you should also be handed the document evidencing the guarantee attached to your particular payments.
Consequences of skipping it
Failing to put the guarantee in place is treated as a consumer-protection infringement, carrying a penalty of up to 25% of the amounts that should have been secured, on top of anything the regional building rules impose.
The Part Most Guides Omit
## The guarantee starts at the building licence
The obligation to guarantee repayment runs from the point the building licence is obtained -- not from the moment you first pay. This is one of the substantive differences between the current regime and the 1968 law it replaced, and it is the single most practical thing to understand before you reserve.
In plain terms: if you pay a reservation fee on a project whose licence has not yet been granted, that money is not sitting behind the statutory guarantee. It may well be protected by what your contract says instead -- many reservation agreements make the fee refundable during a due-diligence window, and that is a contractual protection, not a legal one. The two are not interchangeable, and only one of them is the same at every developer.
This is not a reason to avoid pre-licence projects. It is a reason to know which category a project is in before you transfer anything, and to have your lawyer read the reservation terms rather than assume the statute covers you. Every project on this site states its licence status in its own trust dossier, in those words, because the distinction changes what your money is standing on.
If It Goes Wrong
## What you can actually recover
If construction does not begin, is not finished within the agreed period, or the habitation certificate is not obtained, you may claim back the amounts paid on account -- including the taxes applied to them -- plus statutory interest. You can either terminate the contract or grant the developer an extension, which is recorded as an additional clause setting the new delivery date.
The practical lesson is that the guarantee is only as useful as the paperwork behind it. Ask for the guarantee document at signing, check it names you and your specific payments, and keep it. A guarantee that exists in principle but was never issued to you is the failure mode this provision was written to prevent.
What It Pays
## What the guarantee actually returns
A guarantee is not compensation for a purchase that went wrong. It is a return of what you handed over, and knowing its edges is what stops it being mistaken for something wider.
Covered
The amounts paid on account, the taxes charged on those amounts, and statutory interest from the date each payment was made.
Not covered
The gain you expected. If the finished market moved while you waited, the guarantee returns your money and not the difference. It restores your position; it does not deliver the bargain.
Also not covered
Costs you incurred around the purchase -- legal fees, travel, a mortgage arrangement fee already paid. Those sit outside the statutory guarantee and belong to whatever your contract says about them.
Checking Yours
## How to confirm yours actually exists
A guarantee that exists at the level of the development is not the same as one issued for your payments. These are the four things to establish, in this order, and none of them requires taking anyone's word for it.
### The licence
Ask whether the building licence has been granted, and for the date. Before that point the statutory guarantee has not yet arisen, however the reservation is described.
### The account
The contract should identify the credit institution and the special account, and your payments should go there rather than to a general company account. Compare the account on the contract with the one on the payment instruction.
### The document
Ask for the certificate or policy that covers your payments specifically. It should name you, name the unit, and state the amounts. A master policy for the development is the frame, not the cover.
### The issuer
Check the insurer or bank named on it is authorised to operate in Spain. This takes one search and it is the step people skip.
Keep the document. The failure this provision was written to prevent is not a developer refusing to pay -- it is a buyer discovering, years later, that nothing was ever issued in their name.
If It Fails
## Why you are not a creditor in a queue
This is the part that explains the whole design. If a developer becomes insolvent, unsecured creditors line up against whatever the estate holds, and that process is slow and rarely whole.
A guaranteed buyer is not in that queue. The claim runs against the insurer or the bank that issued the guarantee, which is a solvent third party with its own obligation to you, and it does not depend on what the developer has left. That is the difference the paperwork buys, and it is why a guarantee held in your own name matters more than a reassurance that the development is covered.
Common Questions
## What buyers ask us about guarantees
Is my reservation fee guaranteed?
Only once the building licence has been granted. Paid before that, it rests on the wording of your reservation agreement instead, which is a contractual protection rather than a statutory one, and it differs between developers.
Who pays for the guarantee?
The developer. It is their obligation and their cost, and it should not appear as a charge added to your payments. If it does, ask what it is.
What if the developer refuses to give me the document?
That is a reason to stop rather than to press on. The obligation to hand it over sits with them, and a developer who will not produce it at signing is telling you something about how the rest of the purchase will go.
Does the guarantee cover a delay, or only non-delivery?
It is triggered where construction does not begin, is not finished within the agreed period, or the habitation certificate is not obtained. A delay that runs past the agreed period reaches it; a delay inside that period is a contract question.
Does it transfer if I assign the contract?
Not automatically in the sense that matters. Where a contract is assigned, the guarantee has to follow the new buyer in writing, and that is a step to confirm rather than assume.
Before You Rely On This
## Sourced from the consolidated statute
The obligations described on this page are taken from the first additional provision of Ley 38/1999 as consolidated after Ley 20/2015, and are current as of August 2026. This is general information about how the protection is structured; it is not legal advice, and how it applies to a particular contract is a question for your own lawyer. pages.text:
##
Buying from Abroad · 2026 Guide
What you actually have to be here for
Most of a new-build purchase can be done from where you already live. Three things cannot be done by email, and knowing which three is the difference between a smooth purchase and a delayed one.
Written by Sasan Raftari · Updated 28 August 2026
Comparing projects, reviewing floorplans and prices, even a private presentation of a development, all happen remotely. What cannot happen by email is the part that involves the Spanish state and your bank: a tax number, a signature the notary will accept, and money that arrives from a source you can evidence. Each of those has a lead time, and each of them delays a purchase when it is started late rather than early.
Ask What Your Purchase Needs
How Buying a New-Build Works
The NIE
## The number everything else waits for
An NIE, Número de Identificación de Extranjero, is a tax identification number required for any property purchase in Spain by a non-Spanish national. It is not a residence permit and it does not make you a tax resident. It is an identifier, and without one the purchase cannot be registered in your name.
It is needed before you sign the private purchase contract, not at the deed, which is earlier than most buyers assume. Applications are made in person, either at a Spanish consulate in your own country or in Spain, and a representative acting under a power of attorney can apply on your behalf. Which of those routes is quickest depends on your consulate rather than on any general rule, so the sequence to follow is: ask what your consulate currently requires, then start.
01
### What it is
A tax identifier for foreign nationals, required for the purchase to be registered in your name. Not a residence permit, and not a declaration of tax residency.
02
### When it is needed
Before the private purchase contract, which on an off-plan purchase comes weeks after reservation rather than months.
03
### Who can apply
You, in person, or a representative holding a power of attorney that covers it. Both routes are ordinary; the choice is usually about timing.
Power of Attorney
## The document that makes the rest remote
A power of attorney, a poder , authorises someone in Spain to act for you within limits you set. In a property purchase that is usually your lawyer, and it is what allows a contract to be signed and a deed to be completed while you are elsewhere. It is the single document that decides whether the purchase needs you in the country.
It is signed before a notary. Signed in Spain, that is the end of it. Signed outside Spain, it generally needs to be legalised for use in Spain and translated, and that adds time rather than difficulty. The scope matters more than the mechanics: a power drawn for one specific purchase is a different document from a general one, and your lawyer should be drafting it to the narrower shape.
Signed in Spain
Before a Spanish notary, in one appointment, usually on the same trip as a viewing.
Signed abroad
Before a notary where you live, then legalised for use in Spain and translated. Plan for it rather than around it.
Scope
Specific to the purchase, not general. Ask to read what it authorises before you sign it.
Proof of Funds
## Where the money came from, on paper
Spanish banks, notaries and lawyers are required to establish the origin of the funds in a property purchase. This is routine, it applies to everyone, and it is not a judgement about you. It becomes a problem only when it is left until the week of the deed, because the evidence often has to come from institutions in another country and on their timetable.
The practical version: whatever the money's history is, it should be documentable from the account it leaves. A sale, a transfer between your own accounts, an inheritance, a bonus. Assemble that early, and the question is answered when it is asked rather than sending you back to a bank abroad at the worst possible moment.
Moving the Money
## Getting it there, and to the right account
Two things matter here and they are separate. The first is where the money goes. On an off-plan purchase, payments made before completion must reach the special account named in your contract, not a general company account. That is a legal requirement rather than an administrative preference, and it is covered in full in what actually protects your money .
The second is what it costs to get there. A staged purchase paid from a currency other than the euro is a series of conversions rather than one, spread across the build, and the schedule says nothing about that. How off-plan payments are staged sets out the timing that exposure follows.
A Spanish bank account is not strictly required to complete a purchase, which surprises people. It becomes necessary afterwards, because community fees, IBI and utilities are collected by direct debit from a Spanish account. Opening one takes an NIE, so the sequence runs in the order this page does.
In Practice
## What is genuinely worth being here for
With a power of attorney in place, a purchase can complete without you setting foot in Spain. That is worth knowing, and it is not always worth doing. Two moments repay a trip more than any document does.
01
### Seeing the setting
Not the show home. The road in, the noise at the hour you would actually be there, how far the shops really are. A renderer cannot put those in an image and a floorplan cannot hold them.
02
### Handover
The walkthrough where defects are written down. The date on that record starts the warranty periods, so it is the appointment with the longest tail. Why that date matters .
Before You Rely On This
## Procedure changes, and it varies by consulate
This page describes how a purchase from abroad is structured, not the current paperwork of any one consulate. Requirements, appointment availability and the exact documents differ between countries and change without much notice, and the only reliable version is the one your own consulate publishes today. Nueva Living confirms what a specific purchase requires and coordinates the sequence with your lawyer.
Common Questions
## What buyers ask us about buying remotely
Can I buy a property in Spain without going there?
Yes, with a power of attorney authorising someone in Spain to sign for you. It is ordinary practice rather than a workaround. Whether it is the right choice is a separate question, and it usually turns on whether you have seen the setting rather than on the paperwork.
When do I need the NIE?
Before the private purchase contract, not at the deed. On an off-plan purchase that contract follows the reservation by a matter of weeks, so the application is worth starting as soon as you reserve rather than once the contract is drafted.
Do I need a Spanish bank account to buy?
Not to complete the purchase itself. You will want one afterwards, because community fees, IBI and utilities are collected by direct debit from a Spanish account. Opening one requires an NIE, which is why the two run in that order.
Why is my lawyer asking where my money came from?
Because they are required to establish it, as are the notary and the bank. It applies to every buyer and says nothing about you. The only real risk is leaving it late, since the evidence often has to come from an institution in another country on their schedule rather than yours.
Can my lawyer apply for the NIE for me?
A representative holding a power of attorney that covers it can apply on your behalf. Which route is faster, that or an appointment at your own consulate, depends on the consulate rather than on any general rule, so it is worth asking before choosing.
Does buying property in Spain make me a tax resident?
No. An NIE is an identifier, not a residence permit, and owning a home does not by itself make you resident. Tax residency turns on your own circumstances and is a question for a tax adviser rather than for a property page.

##
Buying from the Netherlands · 2026 Guide
Buying from the Netherlands, what is different
Most of a Costa del Sol purchase can be arranged from home. This page covers what is specific to a Dutch buyer: where the NIE is applied for, what a representative needs, and which tax questions belong with your own adviser.
Written by Sasan Raftari · Updated 18 October 2026
Comparing projects, floorplans and payment schedules, even a private presentation of a development, all happen remotely. The parts that involve the Spanish state are a tax number, a power of attorney and the origin of your funds, and our general guide to buying from abroad explains each of them. This page adds only what changes when you live in the Netherlands.
Ask About Buying From the Netherlands
Buying From Abroad: The General Guide
The NIE

##
How to Buy a New-Build on the Costa del Sol · 7 Steps for 2026
Buying a new-build home, step by step
Off-plan and new-build purchases work differently from buying a resale home. Here is exactly how the process runs, from your first shortlist to collecting the keys.
Written by Sasan Raftari · Updated 12 August 2026
New-build and off-plan purchases follow a different sequence from a resale purchase: staged payments, a private purchase contract, and a developer's construction timeline rather than an immediate move-in date. Seven steps, start to finish.
See the Full Journey
Speak With an Advisor
7 Steps, Reservation to Keys
3 People Involved: You, Nueva Living, Your Lawyer
NIE Needed Before You Sign
2–4 Weeks, Reservation to Contract
The Buying Journey
## Seven steps, start to finish
01
### Work Out What You Actually Want
Be clear on budget, area, property type and timing before looking at a single project. Off-plan homes can be sold years before delivery, so timing matters here more than for a resale purchase.
What You Do Decide your budget, preferred areas, property type and rough timing.
What Nueva Living Does Helps you weigh off-plan against a completed, move-in-ready home for your situation.
Good to know: off-plan or completed?
Off-plan usually means a lower entry price and payments staged over the build period, at the cost of waiting. A completed home costs more upfront but you can see and move into it now. See our full off-plan vs resale comparison for the detail.
02
### Build a Real Shortlist
Property portals tend to show broad price ranges and renders rather than confirmed, current availability. A useful shortlist compares a small number of genuinely suitable projects on the details that matter.
What You Do Share your budget, areas and requirements.
What Nueva Living Does Compares confirmed current pricing, availability and developer track record across projects for you.
Good to know: do I need to be in Spain to start?
No. Most of this stage -- comparing projects, reviewing floorplans and pricing, even a private cinematic presentation of a project -- can be done remotely before you commit to a viewing trip.
03
### View the Projects
For off-plan projects this usually means visiting the site and a show apartment if one exists. For completed developments, you view the actual residence you would be buying.
What You Do Plan and attend the viewing trip, or a remote presentation first.
What Nueva Living Does Arranges viewings and show apartments, ideally two or three projects on one trip for real comparison.
04
### Reserve Your Chosen Residence
A reservation takes the specific residence off the market while your private purchase contract is prepared, typically within two to four weeks.
What You Do Pay the reservation amount, which is later credited against the purchase price.
What Nueva Living Does Confirms the reservation terms and what happens to the amount if you do not proceed.
Good to know: how much is the reservation?
It varies by developer and project, from a few thousand euros up to around 1% of the price on some developments. A reservation is not the point of no return, but it is a real commitment -- confirm the terms before you pay it.
05
### Sign the Private Purchase Contract
The binding agreement setting out price, payment schedule, specification and delivery terms. You will need an NIE before or shortly after this stage.
What You Do Obtain your NIE if you do not already have one, and review the contract.
What Nueva Living Does Coordinates the paperwork and timeline with the developer.
What Your Lawyer Does Reviews the contract terms and confirms the bank guarantee before you sign.
Good to know: what if the developer does not finish the project?
For off-plan purchases, payments from this point are usually staged across construction milestones. Spanish law requires developers to bank-guarantee off-plan payments made before completion, so staged payments are protected if the development is not delivered -- confirming that guarantee is in place is one of the checks your lawyer carries out.
06
### Legal Checks and Independent Representation
We strongly recommend independent legal representation -- a lawyer acting for you, not the developer or the selling agency.
What You Do Instruct an independent lawyer before signing anything binding.
What Nueva Living Does Can introduce you to independent lawyers experienced in Costa del Sol property.
What Your Lawyer Does Checks the developer's registration and track record, the building licence, land registry status and the bank guarantee.
Good to know: financing
Many non-resident buyers arrange a mortgage at this stage. Spanish banks do lend to non-residents, usually financing a portion of the price, though exact terms depend on the bank and your financial profile.
07
### Completion and Handover
Completion happens at the notary, where the final balance is paid and the deed of sale is signed and registered in your name.
What You Do Pay the final balance and sign at the notary.
What Nueva Living Does Coordinates handover and helps you inspect the property against the agreed specification.
What Your Lawyer Does Confirms the deed of sale and its registration.
Good to know: warranties and ongoing costs
Spanish building law generally provides for a structural warranty, a shorter warranty on installations, and a one-year warranty on finishes. After completion, budgeting for ongoing costs such as community fees and annual property tax (IBI) becomes part of owning the home. For the one-off taxes and fees due at purchase, see our breakdown of new-build purchase costs in Andalucia .

## A quick checklist
