Decide off-plan or completed
Apply for your NIE
Select an independent lawyer
Consider a Spanish bank account
Prepare proof of funds
Clarify how you will use the property
Key Terms
## A short glossary
NIE
Numero de Identificacion de Extranjero -- a Spanish tax ID number required for any property purchase by a non-Spanish national.
Reservation Agreement
The document and payment that takes a specific residence off the market while your private purchase contract is prepared.
Private Purchase Contract
Contrato de compraventa -- the binding agreement setting out price, payment schedule, specification and delivery terms.
Bank Guarantee
Legally required protection for off-plan payments made before completion, covering you if the development is not delivered.
Notary
The public official before whom the final deed of sale is signed at completion.
Escritura
The deed of sale signed at the notary and registered in your name at completion.
Land Registry
The official record of property ownership and charges, checked by your lawyer before you sign.
FAQ
## Common buyer questions
Can foreigners buy property in Spain?
Yes. There are no restrictions on non-Spanish nationals buying property in Spain, whether as a resident or non-resident.
What is an NIE number and do I need one?
An NIE (Numero de Identificacion de Extranjero) is a tax ID number required for any property purchase in Spain by a non-Spanish national. Nueva Living can guide you through obtaining one before you reserve.
What costs should I budget for on top of the purchase price?
Buyers typically budget for transfer tax or VAT, notary fees, land registry fees and legal fees on top of the purchase price. Nueva Living provides a full, current cost breakdown for your chosen residence before you reserve.
Can I get a mortgage in Spain as a non-resident?
Many Spanish banks offer mortgages to non-resident buyers, typically financing a portion of the purchase price. Exact terms depend on the bank and your personal financial profile.
What is the difference between off-plan and completed properties?
Off-plan means the development is still under construction and is usually sold with staged payments through to completion. A completed property is ready to view and move into now.
How does the reservation and payment process work?
Reservation and payment structures vary by development and are set out in full before you reserve. Nueva Living reconfirms the current schedule for your chosen residence at every step.
Can I rent out the property after purchase?
This depends on the individual development and local regulations, which can vary by community and municipality. Nueva Living will confirm the specific rules for a development before you reserve.
Do I need a lawyer?
Yes, we strongly recommend independent legal representation for any property purchase in Spain. Nueva Living can put you in touch with independent lawyers experienced in Costa del Sol property.

##
Mortgages with Habeno · 2026 Guide
Financing your home with Habeno
Nueva Living has partnered with Habeno, a mortgage broker for international buyers in Spain. This is what that partnership is, how their process runs, and what is worth settling before you apply.
Written by Sasan Raftari · Updated 14 October 2026
We help international buyers find and compare new-build and off-plan homes on the Costa del Sol. Financing is the other half of many purchases, and it is a separate service, so we work with Habeno, a mortgage broker that arranges Spanish mortgages for international buyers and compares offers from several banks on your behalf. This page describes that service as Habeno describes it, and explains where our part ends and theirs begins.
See Your Mortgage Options
Estimate Your Payment First
The Partnership
## Two companies, two jobs
Nueva Living finds and compares homes, and guides you through the purchase. Habeno is a different company that arranges the mortgage: it prepares your application, sends it to several Spanish banks and coordinates the process with the lender, the appraiser and the notary. The mortgage itself is an agreement between you and the bank you choose, not with us and not with Habeno.
You do not have to use Habeno to buy a home through us. It is the broker we work with, and the one this page describes, and you are free to arrange financing with your own bank or another broker.
What Habeno Offers
## One application, several banks
These are the three things Habeno says its service gives an international buyer, in our words. We have not tested its offers against other lenders, and nothing here is a promise of what a bank will lend.
01
### Bank comparison
One application reaches several leading Spanish banks, so the offers can be compared side by side and used against each other when negotiating.
02
### A named advisor
A senior advisor who specialises in international buyers coordinates the parties involved in a Spanish mortgage: the banks, lawyers, notaries and appraisers.
03
### Tailored financing
The structure and terms are meant to be fitted to your own financial situation, with the terms made clear before you commit.
The Process
## Four steps, and how long each one takes
The timings below are the ones Habeno publishes on its partner page, as read in October 2026. They are Habeno's estimates, they depend on the bank and on how complete your documents are, and they are not a commitment from us.
1 · Pre-approval
A digital pre-approval so you know where you stand early. Habeno quotes pre-approval within 24 hours, a loan offer within one to two weeks and full approval in about six to eight weeks.
2 · Documents
Your advisor helps you collect and verify the documents, then submits the full application to several banks.
3 · Offers
You review the offers side by side with your advisor and choose one. Habeno then notifies the selected bank.
4 · Closing
Habeno arranges the appraisal, handles the legal paperwork and the FEIN, and schedules the notary signing.
The FEIN, the Ficha Europea de Información Normalizada , is the standardised sheet in which a Spanish lender sets out the terms of its offer. It is the document to read closely, because it is what the bank is offering rather than what anyone has summarised.
The Pre-Assessment
## What the first form asks you for
Habeno describes the first step as a free pre-assessment that takes about two minutes, in three parts: the loan, your personal details, and the partner and consent step. The loan part asks for five things.
### The price
The estimated price of the property. Our project pages list prices before taxes, so add them: what a new-build costs on top of the price .
### The loan
How much you want to borrow, and how much of your own funds you have available. The second number matters as much as the first.
### The type of purchase
Second home, off-plan, new development or self-build. Say which one you are buying, because the answer shapes how the financing is arranged.
### Reservation
Whether you have already reserved a property. The form asks the question; the page we read does not say that a reservation is required.
The last step of the form is a partner and consent step. Read it before you submit: it is the text that governs how your details are shared, and it is Habeno's to state rather than ours.
Before You Apply
## Settle these first
### Your own funds
Decide what you will contribute and where it comes from. A bank will want the origin of the money documented, and it is easier to assemble early. Where the money came from, on paper .
### The payment schedule
An off-plan purchase is paid in stages, and the stages come before the deed. Compare the dates against Habeno's six to eight weeks for full approval before you reserve. How off-plan payments are staged .
### Your deposit protection
Money you pay during construction is protected on terms that start at a specific point in the timeline, which is separate from the mortgage. How the bank guarantee works .
### A planning number
Our calculator gives a rough payment and cash-needed figure from typical non-resident terms. It is a planning tool, not an offer. Open the calculator .
What This Page Does Not Tell You
## No rates, no approval odds
We do not publish interest rates, loan-to-value limits or fees here, because Habeno's partner page does not state any and we will not borrow figures from elsewhere. What a bank will lend you depends on the bank, on your income and on your circumstances, and the only figures that count are the ones in your own FEIN.
Nueva Living is a new-build advisory, not a financial adviser, and this page is general information rather than financial advice. Habeno's fees, its terms of service and its handling of your data are set by Habeno, so ask it directly before you apply.
See Your Mortgage Options
Ask Us a Question First
Common Questions
## What buyers ask us about financing
Do I have to use Habeno to buy through Nueva Living?
No. Habeno is the mortgage broker we work with, and you can arrange financing through your own bank or another broker.
Does Habeno charge for its service?
Habeno's partner page calls the pre-assessment free and does not state what the rest of the service costs. Ask Habeno for its fees in writing before you commit to anything.
Is the pre-approval a loan offer?
No. By Habeno's own sequence, pre-approval comes first, a loan offer follows within one to two weeks, and full approval comes later still. A bank is bound only by the offer and the approval it actually issues.
Can I start before I have chosen a home?
The form asks whether you have reserved a property, but the page we read does not make that a condition. The estimated price it asks for is easier to give once you have shortlisted a project, so it is a reasonable moment to ask us for one.

At the time of writing, Habeno's partner page and form are published in English. If you would rather go through the questions with someone first, ask us.
How does this fit with an off-plan payment schedule?
The two run on different clocks. The schedule sets when you pay the developer, and the mortgage process has its own lead time, which Habeno puts at about six to eight weeks for full approval. Line the two up before you reserve, and ask us for the schedule of the project you are considering.

## Listed prices, not sale prices
Every figure on this page is a developer’s current list price for a new-build project on the Costa del Sol, read from the project files behind this site. Each project is represented by its from price, the lowest price in its published price list, and the tables compare those prices by area, by type of home and by delivery year.
These are asking prices of homes still for sale, not prices paid and not a price per square metre. A from price is the cheapest home in a project and says nothing about the rest of it. The method, including how tax is treated, is set out at the end of the page.

Method
## How the figures are produced
What is counted
Every published project with a listed price and an area that is not archived. Projects are not weighted by size or by number of homes.
From price
The lowest price in the developer’s current price list for the project, as transcribed on its page. A list price for the cheapest home: not an average, not a typical home and not a sale price.
Tax
Prices are compared as each developer publishes them. Tax stated as excluded: 110. Stated as included: 0. Not stated: 21. Our guide to purchase costs sets out IVA at 10% and AJD at 1.2% on a new-build, 11.2% in taxes, before notary, registry and legal fees.
Purchase costs in Andalucia
Statistics
Lowest, median and highest are taken across the projects’ from prices. With an even number of projects the median is the mean of the middle two, rounded to the euro.
Types and delivery
Types are the property types each project publishes; duplexes count as apartments and duplex penthouses as penthouses. Delivery is the quarter or year the developer states.
Data date
Prices were last checked between May 2026 and November 2026. The page is rebuilt from the project files whenever the site is built.
Not included
Price per square metre, sale or transaction prices, resale homes, rental yields and return projections. Nueva Living provides current, factual information rather than return projections.
Common Questions
## Questions about these figures
What does a from price mean?
It is the lowest price in a developer’s published price list for a project, for the cheapest home listed. It shows where a project starts, not what a typical home in it costs, and the tax column of the project table shows how each price is stated.
Why do prices differ so much between areas?
Part of the answer is what is being built. Projects selling only villas have a median from price of €2,375,000, against €495,000 for projects selling only apartments. Size, plot, setting and specification also differ, and a from price does not capture them.
Are these the prices buyers pay?
No. They are developers’ list prices, which can change without notice, not transaction prices. Nueva Living confirms the current price and availability of a home in writing before any reservation.
How often is this page updated?
The figures are produced from the project files each time the site is built, so a change to a project’s price list reaches this page with the next build. Each project page shows when its price was last checked; the checks behind this edition run from May 2026 to November 2026.

##
New-Build Warranties and Snagging · 2026 Guide
Three warranties, three different clocks
A Spanish new-build carries ten, three and one-year cover against defects. They start on the same day, point at different parties, and only one of them is insured by law.
Written by Sasan Raftari · Updated 24 August 2026
A new-build comes with statutory cover against defects, and it is not one warranty but three, each running for a different length of time and each pointing at a different party. Knowing which clock applies to a given problem is what turns a snagging list from a favour the developer might do into a claim with a legal basis.
The Three Periods
Ask About a Specific Project
Article 17, Ley 38/1999
## Ten years, three years, one year
All three periods run from the date the works are formally received without reservations -- or, where reservations were made, from the date those are put right. Not from when you move in, and not from the deed.
10 years · structural
Damage caused by defects affecting the foundations, supports, beams, floor slabs, load-bearing walls or other structural elements. The building agents are liable.
3 years · habitability
Damage from defects in construction elements or installations that cause the building to fail the habitability requirements -- damp penetration, insulation, water, heating and similar.
1 year · finishes
Defects of execution affecting elements of finish or trim. Here the constructor alone is liable, which is a narrower answer than the other two periods give you.
Insurance
## Only one of the three is insured by law
Liability and insurance are not the same thing, and this is where expectations often run ahead of the statute. For buildings whose main use is housing, only the ten-year structural cover is compulsory insurance. The one-year and three-year guarantees remain liabilities of the parties rather than insurances that must be in place, pending implementing regulation that has not arrived.
In practice this means a structural problem has an insurer standing behind it, while a three-year habitability defect is a claim against the agents involved. Both are real; they are not equally easy to enforce, and it is worth knowing which one you are in before a dispute rather than during it.
At Handover
## The snagging list is the clock-starter
Because the periods run from reception of the works, and because reservations noted at reception shift the start date until they are put right, the handover inspection is not a formality. Recording defects in writing at that point is what fixes the date and creates the record you would later rely on.
Snagging inspections themselves are market practice rather than a statutory step -- there is no law requiring one, and no prescribed format. What the law does is define the periods and the liabilities that an inspection lets you use. A written, dated list, delivered to the developer, is the practical bridge between the two.
Who Answers
## Who you can actually claim against
"The building agents" is a category, not an address. It covers the developer, the constructor, the architect who designed it and the technical architect who supervised the work, and each of them answers for their own part.
The practical point is the one buyers rarely hear: where the responsibility for a defect cannot be apportioned between them, they answer jointly and severally -- and the developer answers jointly with all of them in any case. You do not have to establish which professional caused a problem before you can raise it. You raise it with the developer, and the apportioning is theirs to work out.
The Second Clock
## Two years to act on it
There are two timers, and confusing them is the most expensive mistake available here.
The cover
Ten, three or one year from reception of the works. This is the window in which a defect has to appear to be covered at all.
The claim
Two years from when the damage appears, to bring the action. A defect that shows up in year nine is covered, and the claim for it still has to be brought within two years of showing up.
What that means
Noticing a crack and waiting to see whether it worsens can move you out of time while the ten-year cover is still running. Record the date you saw it and start the conversation then.
In Practice
## What to do when you find one
Most defects are resolved by the developer without any of the above being invoked. The steps below are what keep that route open and the formal one available if it closes.
### Date it
Photograph it with something that fixes the date, and write down when you first saw it. The two-year clock runs from the damage appearing, and your own record is usually the only evidence of when that was.
### Report it in writing
Email is enough to start. What matters is that a dated record exists showing you raised it and when, rather than a phone call neither side can later describe the same way.
### Do not repair it first
Fixing a defect before it has been inspected removes the evidence of what it was. Make it safe if it needs making safe, and document the state it was in.
### Get it looked at
For anything structural, an independent technical report is what turns "there is a crack" into a description of a cause. It is also what a claim would be built on if one becomes necessary.
Common Questions
## What buyers ask us about defects
Does the warranty transfer if I sell?
The cover attaches to the building rather than to you, so a buyer who acquires within the periods inherits what is left of them. It is worth telling them the reception date, since that is where their remaining time is measured from.
What counts as structural?
Damage from defects affecting foundations, supports, beams, floor slabs, load-bearing walls and similar elements. Cracked tiling is not structural because it is unpleasant; a crack that traces to movement in the structure is, and telling those apart is what a technical report does.
Who pays for the snagging inspection?
You do, where you engage someone independent, and it is usually money well spent. The developer's own handover walkthrough is not the same exercise and is not conducted in your interest.
What if the developer no longer exists?
For the ten-year structural cover, this is precisely why the insurance is compulsory: the claim runs against the insurer. For the one and three-year periods, which are liabilities rather than insurances, a dissolved developer is a genuine practical problem, and that is worth knowing before it is one.
Can I refuse to complete because of defects?
That depends on their severity and on your contract, and it is a question for your lawyer rather than a rule. What is generally available is completing with reservations recorded, which shifts the start of the periods until those are put right.

##
Off-Plan Payment Schedules · 2026 Guide
How off-plan payments are actually staged
Not an averaged range borrowed from elsewhere: the schedules the developers of the projects on this site have supplied in writing.
Written by Sasan Raftari · Updated 24 August 2026
Off-plan purchases are paid in stages, and the stages are not standardised. The figures below are not a market average taken from elsewhere -- they are the actual schedules supplied by the developers of the projects listed on this site, which is why the ranges are narrower and less tidy than the ones you will read in a generic guide.
The Four Stages
See the Developments
What We Actually See
## Reservation, contract, build, deed
Across the projects on this site where the developer has supplied a written schedule, the shape is consistent even though the numbers move.
Reservation
Either a fixed sum or a percentage. We see fixed reservations from €6,000 to €10,000, and percentage reservations from 1% to 5%. This takes the unit off the market for an agreed period while contracts are prepared.
Private purchase contract
Typically bringing the total paid to 30%, with the reservation usually counted towards it. Some developers stage this as 25% at contract with the balance spread across the build. Signing windows are short -- 15 to 30 days from reservation is normal.
During construction
Highly variable. Some projects take nothing between contract and completion; others take 10% at a fixed date, or tie payments to certified milestones such as completion of the foundation and of the structure. One project on this site spreads 50% across fifteen monthly payments from the start of works.
Completion
The balance at the deed of sale, most often 50% to 70%. This is also where the bulk of the tax falls due.
Note that stage payments are quoted plus VAT in most schedules, so the cash required at each stage is higher than the headline percentage. See what a new-build costs on top of the price for how IVA and AJD land across the timeline.
Reservation Agreements
## Market practice, not statute
This is worth stating plainly, because it is often blurred: there is no Spanish statute governing reservation agreements. What your reservation fee does, whether it is refundable, and for how long, is whatever your particular reservation document says. It is a contract, and its terms vary between developers.
That matters more than it sounds, because the statutory guarantee over advance payments only begins once the building licence has been obtained. A reservation paid before that point rests on the contract wording alone. Some agreements make the fee refundable for a defined due-diligence window; others do not. Read it, or have your lawyer read it, before transferring anything -- and see how the bank guarantee works for what changes once the licence is in place.
Where The Money Sits
## Not the developer's working capital
Once the guarantee regime applies, amounts you pay on account must be received through a credit institution and held in a special account, separate from any other class of funds, and may only be drawn for costs arising directly from building those homes. If a developer proposes any other arrangement for staged payments, that is the point to stop and take advice.
The Real Number
## What 30% at contract actually costs
Schedules are quoted net of VAT, so every percentage on them understates the transfer by a tenth. On a €600,000 home the difference is not academic.
Reservation
€10,000, usually counted towards the next stage rather than added to it.
At contract, 30%
€180,000 net, less the €10,000 already paid, plus 10% IVA on the €180,000. The transfer is €188,000, not €170,000.
At the deed, 70%
€420,000 net plus IVA on that, plus the AJD on the full price, plus notary, registry and legal. Around €476,000 before fees.
Read a schedule as net figures and add a tenth to each. A plan that looks like 30/70 is closer to 33/77 of the price in cash terms, and that is the number to hold against your own liquidity.
Before Signing
## What to check in the schedule itself
Two schedules can quote identical percentages and behave completely differently, because what triggers a payment is set by wording rather than by the number beside it.
### What triggers each stage
A date is a promise. A certified construction milestone -- foundation complete, structure complete -- is an event someone signs off. Milestone-linked schedules move with the build; date-linked ones ask you to pay on time whether or not the build did.
### Who certifies it
Where payments follow milestones, the schedule should say who confirms one has been reached. In practice that is the project's technical architect, and the certificate is a document you can ask to see.
### How much notice you get
Fifteen days is common, and it is short if funds have to move across borders. Establish the notice period before you sign rather than discovering it with a payment demand.
### What happens if you are late
Contracts vary widely: interest, a cure period, and in some cases termination with retention of part of what you have paid. This is one of the clauses worth reading closely, because it is the one that costs the most when it applies.
Currency and Timing
## The cost that is not in the schedule
If your money is not in euros, a staged purchase is a series of conversions rather than one, and the schedule says nothing about that.
A build running two or three years means four or five transfers, each at whatever the rate is that week. Buyers who fix the rate forward for known dates trade the chance of a better rate for a known number, which is a decision worth taking deliberately rather than by default. Where the schedule is milestone-linked rather than date-linked, forward cover is harder to arrange, and that is a real argument for asking which kind you are being offered.
Common Questions
## What buyers ask us about payments
Can I negotiate the payment schedule?
Sometimes, and more often on the timing than the totals. Developers with financing tied to pre-sales have less room than those releasing later phases. It is always worth asking, and the answer tells you something about the project either way.
Can I pay more upfront for a discount?
Occasionally offered, and worth weighing carefully: paying ahead of the schedule increases what you have at risk before delivery, and the guarantee covers what you have paid rather than what you were promised in return.
What if I cannot make a stage payment?
Tell the developer before the date rather than after. Most contracts allow for a cure period and interest, and a conversation held early is a different conversation from one held after a default has been declared.
Do stage payments go to the developer directly?
They should go to the special account named in your contract, held apart from the developer's other funds, once the guarantee regime applies. Compare the account on the contract against the one on the payment instruction each time.
Does a longer schedule mean a better deal?
Not by itself. Spreading payments helps your cash flow and increases the period over which you are exposed to the build completing. Which matters more depends on your own position, not on the shape of the schedule.
Before You Rely On This
## Schedules change per project
The ranges above describe the written schedules held for the projects listed on this site as of August 2026. They are not a rule, and they are not an offer -- an individual developer can and does structure payments differently, and terms change between releases. Nueva Living reconfirms the current payment structure in writing for a specific residence before any reservation.

##
Off-Plan vs Resale on the Costa del Sol · 2026 Guide
Off-plan vs resale: which fits your plan
Both are legitimate ways to buy on the Costa del Sol. The right one depends on your timeline, your appetite for construction risk, and what you actually want the property to do for you.
Written by Sasan Raftari · Updated 12 August 2026
Neither is inherently the better investment -- they suit different buyers, timelines and risk tolerances. Compare them below on the points that actually affect your decision.
Compare Now
Speak With an Advisor
Side by Side
## Off-plan or completed
Price
Usually priced below a comparable finished home, since you are committing years ahead of delivery and taking on construction timeline risk. That gap narrows, or closes, as a project moves toward its final released units.
Payment
Staged: a reservation, a larger payment on signing the private purchase contract, further payments at construction milestones, and the balance on completion.
Risk
Construction and delivery risk: the project could be delayed or, worst case, not completed. Payments made before completion are required by law to be bank-guaranteed.
Specification
Buying early sometimes means a genuine say in finishes -- flooring, kitchen options, occasionally layout -- depending how far along construction is. That window closes near completion.
Timing
Waiting, sometimes years, for delivery. The developer's track record for hitting its delivery date deserves real scrutiny.
Appreciation
The case is buying below completed-market price and the value closing that gap by delivery. This depends on the specific project and area performing as expected -- it is not a guarantee.
Snagging
A formal snagging inspection happens before or at handover, with defects listed for the developer to fix under the build warranty. You are working from the developer's finish standard, not judging an existing property.
Documentation
Completion depends on the developer obtaining the first occupation license and certificate of completion before the deed can be signed at the notary. Your lawyer confirms these are in place before you complete.
Completion
Happens once the building is finished and licensed, on a date the developer estimates rather than guarantees. Delays of a few months against the original estimate are not unusual.
Price
Costs more upfront, but you are paying for a known quantity: the actual finish, the actual view, the actual noise level, none of which you can fully judge from a floorplan and a render.
Payment
Simpler: reserve, sign, pay the balance, usually within 30 to 60 days. No construction-linked schedule, and no way to spread the cost over time.
Risk
Removed entirely. What you see is what you get, and you can inspect the actual property before committing to anything.
Specification
Fixed. A limitation if you wanted something different, an advantage if you would rather judge real materials and workmanship than a specification sheet.
Timing
Can generate rental income or be lived in immediately after completion, with no construction timeline in the way.
Appreciation
Easier to benchmark against genuinely comparable recent sales in the same building or area -- real, current data rather than a projection.
Snagging
Not applicable in the same way. Any defects are whatever the current owner has or has not addressed, so a professional survey before you commit matters more here than a developer warranty.
Documentation
Already issued and checkable: your lawyer verifies the existing title, license history and any charges on the property at the Land Registry before you sign.
Completion
Set by you and the seller, typically 30 to 60 days after signing, with no construction or licensing timeline to depend on.
### Does the bank guarantee cover everything I pay?
It covers payments made ahead of completion specifically. The exact scope and validity of the guarantee for a given project is something to confirm in writing before signing, not something to assume.
## Which one actually fits you
Off-plan tends to suit buyers who do not need the property immediately, want to spread payments over time, and are comfortable with construction-stage risk in exchange for a lower entry price and, in some cases, a say in the finish.
A completed home tends to suit buyers who want to move in, rent out, or simply see exactly what they are buying without waiting or without taking on delivery risk -- often at a higher upfront cost for that certainty.
Most buyers are not purely one or the other. The honest way to decide is to compare specific projects against your own budget, timeline and risk tolerance, rather than deciding on off-plan versus resale as an abstract category first. For the full step-by-step process once you have decided, see how buying works .
The Tax Gap
## Four points separate them
Most comparisons stop at the asking price. In Andalucía the two purchases are taxed differently, and the difference is large enough to change which one is actually cheaper.
New-build
IVA at 10% plus AJD at 1.2%, so 11.2% of the price in tax. Both are set by law and neither is negotiable.
Resale
ITP at 7% and no AJD. Four points lower, on the same price.
What it means
A resale at the same headline price costs roughly €18,000 less in tax on a €450,000 purchase. An off-plan unit has to be priced meaningfully below the finished comparable before it is the cheaper transaction, not merely the cheaper number.
That does not settle the question. It does mean the comparison is not the one the asking prices suggest, and it belongs in the arithmetic before anything else.
Resale Risk
## What a resale carries that a new-build does not
Off-plan risk is easy to name: the building might be late. Resale risk is quieter, because it arrives attached to the property rather than to the timeline.
### Debts follow the home
Unpaid community charges attach to the property itself for the current year and the three preceding ones, and unpaid IBI attaches to it without a time limit of that kind. Your lawyer asks for a certificate of no debt from the community and checks the IBI receipts before you sign.
### The 3% retention
Where the seller is not resident in Spain, the buyer withholds 3% of the price and pays it to the tax office on the seller's account. It is the buyer's obligation, not the seller's courtesy, and it does not arise at all buying from a developer.
### Licence history
Extensions, glazed terraces and pool houses added without permission are common and do not always appear in the deed. What is registered, what is built and what was licensed have to agree, and only a search establishes that.
### No warranty behind it
A new-build carries statutory cover against defects. A resale carries whatever remains of the original periods, which on an older home is usually nothing, so a survey does the work a warranty would.
None of this makes resale the worse choice. It makes the diligence different: on off-plan you are checking a developer and a licence, and on a resale you are checking a building and its history.
Common Questions
## What buyers ask us when deciding
Is off-plan actually cheaper?
At the same headline price, no, because the tax is four points higher. Off-plan is cheaper where the price genuinely sits below the finished comparable by more than that, which is a project-by-project question rather than a rule.
Can I get a mortgage on an off-plan purchase?
Yes, but the loan is normally drawn at completion rather than during construction, so the stage payments come out of your own funds. That changes the cash profile more than the total, and it is worth modelling before you reserve.
What happens if the development is delayed?
Delays of a few months against the original estimate are common. Your contract sets the delivery date and what happens if it is missed, including whether you may terminate or grant an extension, and that clause is worth reading before you sign rather than after.
Can I sell an off-plan unit before completion?
Sometimes. Whether the contract can be assigned to another buyer, and on what terms and fee, is set by the developer and varies widely. If that is part of your plan, establish it in writing before reserving, not later.
Which one rents better?
A completed home can be let immediately, which is a real advantage where income matters from day one. Beyond that, letting depends on the specific development's rules and the local licensing regime rather than on whether the home was bought off-plan.
Key Terms
## A short glossary
Private Purchase Contract
Contrato de compraventa -- the binding agreement setting out price, payment schedule, specification and delivery terms, signed after reservation.
Bank Guarantee
Legally required protection for off-plan payments made before completion, covering you if the development is not delivered.
Snagging
A formal inspection before or at handover to list defects for the developer to fix under the build warranty.
First Occupation License
Licencia de primera ocupacion -- the official confirmation a newly built home is fit to be lived in, required before completion.
Comunidad de Propietarios
The community of owners that manages and charges for shared areas and services in a development, whether off-plan or resale.
Escritura
The deed of sale signed at the notary and registered in your name at completion.
The two routes are also taxed differently: new-build carries IVA and AJD, resale carries ITP. See what a new-build actually costs in Andalucia for the figures.

##
New-Build Purchase Costs in Andalucia · 2026 Guide
What a new-build costs on top of the price
Every competitor writes a Spain-wide cost guide quoting 8 to 13 per cent. New-build in Andalucia is a specific number, and it is knowable before you offer.
Written by Sasan Raftari · Updated 24 August 2026
Most cost guides for Spain quote a single national range, usually somewhere between 8 and 13 per cent. That range exists because it is averaging two different purchases across seventeen regions. For a new-build in Andalucía the tax side is not a range at all -- it is two fixed rates, and you can work out the number exactly.
See the Breakdown
Ask About a Specific Project
The Two Taxes
## IVA and AJD, not transfer tax
A new-build bought from the developer is a first transmission, so it carries VAT rather than the transfer tax that applies to a resale. In Andalucía that means two separate taxes on the same purchase.
IVA (VAT)
10% of the purchase price. The national rate for new residential property. It drops to 4% for officially protected housing (VPO de régimen especial), which does not apply to the developments on this site.
AJD (stamp duty)
1.2% of the purchase price in Andalucía. This is the regional rate, set at 1.2% since April 2021 and made permanent by the region's Ley 5/2021. Older guides still quote 1.5%, which was the rate before that change.
Total tax
11.2% on a new-build. For comparison, a resale in Andalucía carries ITP at 7% and no AJD -- so the tax on a new home is roughly four points higher than on an equivalent resale.
Reduced Rates
## When AJD is lower than 1.2%
Andalucía applies reduced AJD rates in specific circumstances. They are worth checking before you assume the general rate, though most purchases on this coast fall outside them.
### 1%
Where the property value does not exceed €150,000 and it will be the buyer's habitual residence.
### 0.3%
Where the buyer is under 35 and the property will be their habitual residence.
### 0.1%
For large families (familia numerosa) and for buyers with a recognised disability, subject to the region's conditions.
On Top of Tax
## Notary, registry and legal fees
Notary and Land Registry fees are set by national tariff, so they do not vary between providers. Legal fees do.
Notary
Roughly €600 to €1,200 on a typical residential purchase, scaling with the price and the length of the deed. Regulated, so shopping around does not change it.
Land Registry
Roughly €400 to €700. Also regulated.
Legal
Typically 1% of the price plus 21% IVA on the fee, or a fixed quote in the €1,500 to €3,000 range for a straightforward purchase. This one is negotiable, and it is the line worth comparing quotes on.
Worked Example
## A €450,000 new-build
IVA at 10%
€45,000
AJD at 1.2%
€5,400
Notary and registry
Roughly €1,000 to €1,900
Legal
Roughly €4,500 plus IVA at 1%, or a fixed quote
Budget for
Around €57,000, or about 12.5% over the price. Taxes are the fixed €50,400 of that; the rest moves with who you instruct.
That is the acquisition cost. It does not include mortgage arrangement and valuation fees if you are borrowing, furnishing, or the running costs that start after completion -- IBI, community fees and utilities.
With a Mortgage
## What a mortgage adds to the total
If you are borrowing, three of the four costs below fall on you and one does not. The one that does not is the one older guides still list as yours.
### Valuation
The tasación, €300 to €600, paid before the bank will issue a binding offer. The report is valid for six months, and the bank lends against the lower of valuation and price.
### Arrangement fee
The comisión de apertura, 0% to 1% of the loan. Negotiable, and often waived on non-resident lending at a conservative loan-to-value.
### AJD on the mortgage
Nothing. The lender has paid the stamp duty on the mortgage deed since Real Decreto-ley 17/2018. Any guide still listing it as a buyer cost predates that change.
### Broker
0.5% to 1% of the loan, or a fixed fee, if you use one. Worth it where a broker reaches lenders that price non-resident files differently.
Non-resident lending on this coast typically runs to 60% or 70% of the lower of price and valuation. The cash you need is the deposit plus everything on this page, not the deposit alone.
When It Falls Due
## The costs do not arrive together
A single percentage makes it sound like one bill at the end. In practice the tax arrives in instalments and the professional fees arrive at the deed.
At reservation
Nothing beyond the reservation fee itself, and that counts towards the price rather than sitting on top of it.
During construction
IVA at 10% is charged on each stage payment as you make it, not held back to completion. This is the line most budgets get wrong: the cash required at each stage is the percentage plus a tenth of it again.
At the deed
The balance of the price, the AJD in full, notary, Land Registry and your lawyer's fee. This is where the largest single transfer happens.
After Completion
## The costs that start rather than stop
Acquisition cost is the number people compare. Running cost is the number they live with, and it is knowable before you reserve.
### IBI
Municipal property tax, charged on the valor catastral rather than the market price, broadly 0.4% to 1.1% of it a year. Because the catastral value is a fraction of what you paid, the bill is usually a few hundred to a couple of thousand euros.
### Community fees
Set per home by participation quota. A development with a spa, heated pools and a concierge costs more to run than a small block, and the community budget exists before you reserve. Ask for it.
### Refuse
The basura charge, billed by the town hall, modest, usually annually or quarterly depending on the municipality.
### Non-resident income tax
Spain taxes an imputed income on a second home even when it is never let, declared on Modelo 210. Residents of the EU and EEA are taxed at 19%, others at 24%.
Common Questions
## What buyers ask us about cost
Is the 11.2% negotiable?
No. IVA is set nationally and AJD by Andalucía, and neither moves on a private purchase. What is negotiable is the legal fee, and the arrangement fee if you borrow.
Do I pay plusvalía municipal?
No. That tax falls on the seller, and on a new-build the seller is the developer. It is a resale question that follows buyers into new-build guides where it does not belong.
Is the IVA paid in one payment at the end?
No. It is charged on each stage payment as that payment is made. A schedule quoting 30% at contract means 30% plus IVA on that 30%, and the same at every stage after it.
What is the 3% retention I keep reading about?
It applies where the seller is a non-resident, which makes it a resale matter. Buying from a Spanish developer it does not arise at all.
Can I reclaim the IVA?
Only where the buyer is a business and the property is put to a taxable activity, and that brings its own obligations. On a home bought privately, no.
Before You Rely On This
## Figures current at August 2026
The IVA rate is national and the AJD rate is set by Andalucía; both can change, and the reduced rates carry conditions that depend on your circumstances. Where a resident might get financing up to 80% of a property's value, non-residents are typically capped closer to 70%, and the exact rate, term and how much of your income counts all vary by bank and by your personal financial profile. On top of the mortgage itself, budget for taxes and purchase costs — transfer tax or VAT, notary, land registry and legal fees — which typically add another 10-13% on top of the purchase price in Spain.

Can foreigners buy property in Spain?

### Apartment
The lower entry price in any given development, and where the value argument for this area is strongest: the price per built square metre here is materially below the equivalent in Marbella. Ground-floor units are often sold with a private garden.

The largest terrace or solarium in the building and the best of the sea or golf view, at a premium over a mid-floor unit. On this coast a penthouse still frequently lands under what a mid-floor apartment costs further west.

## What buyers usually ask us
Why are new-build prices lower here than in Marbella?
Land costs less on this stretch than it does between Marbella and Estepona, and that carries through to the finished price rather than reflecting a difference in build quality. Current releases here run from around EUR 390,000, against EUR 527,500 for the equivalent in Marbella.
How far is Malaga airport?
Closer than it is from Marbella. Fuengirola, Mijas Costa and Benalmadena all sit on the airport side of the coast, which shortens the transfer at both ends of a trip and matters more than it sounds if you plan to visit often or rent the property out.

## Not Estepona, not quite Marbella
The New Golden Mile is the coastal strip running from the eastern edge of Estepona up to Puerto Banús. It is its own market rather than a part of either: buyers who start in Marbella come here for space and newer stock, and buyers who start in Estepona come here for proximity to Puerto Banús.
It is also unusually mixed. Within a few minutes of each other you will find beachside apartment releases from EUR 695,000 and golf-side villa collections up to EUR 3,500,000, which is why this page covers both rather than splitting them. Every current release here is off-plan or under construction with staged payments.
Looking more widely? Our guide to where to buy in Estepona, area by area sets the New Golden Mile against the town itself and the coast further west.

### Buyer Profile
Suits buyers who want Puerto Banús within reach without Marbella pricing, and families who need more built area than the Golden Mile offers.

03
### What Varies Most
Distance to the beach against distance to the golf. The apartment releases sit beachside; the villa collections sit inland around El Campanario.

New Golden Mile in detail

02
### El Campanario
Inland and golf-facing, built around the golf and country club. Almost all of the villa stock on this stretch sits here, on larger plots than anything beachside.
03
### Bel Air
An established, low-density address at the Marbella end of the strip, closest to Puerto Banús, where new villa releases are small and infrequent.

## Apartment or villa on this stretch?

Beachside, walkable and from EUR 695,000. Community pools and gardens are maintained for you, which suits owners who are not here year-round. The practical choice if you want to be able to leave and lock the door.

Common Questions
## What buyers usually ask us
Where exactly is the New Golden Mile?
It is the coastal strip between the eastern edge of Estepona and Puerto Banús, taking in Cancelada, El Campanario and Bel Air. It is not an administrative area, which is why it does not appear on municipal maps, but it is how the stretch is bought and sold locally.
Is it in Estepona or Marbella?
Almost all of it falls within the municipality of Estepona, with the Bel Air end closest to the Marbella boundary. For practical purposes -- taxes, licences, town hall -- treat it as Estepona.
Why is it cheaper than the Golden Mile in Marbella?
It is further from central Marbella and it is newer, with more land still being built on. That is what keeps entry prices near EUR 695,000 here against Marbella pricing a few kilometres east. It is a location difference, not a build-quality one.
Can I walk to the beach from these developments?
From the beachside apartment releases around Cancelada, generally yes. The villa collections around El Campanario are inland and golf-facing, so a car is assumed there. We confirm the actual walking distance for a specific development rather than relying on a brochure claim.
Is there much difference in service charges between an apartment and a villa here?
They are different in kind rather than degree. An apartment carries a community charge covering shared pools, gardens and lighting. A villa usually carries a smaller community charge but takes on its own pool and garden maintenance directly, which often costs more in total once you add it up.

## What buyers usually ask us
How far is San Pedro from Puerto Banús?
About five minutes by car, or a walk along the promenade from the eastern edge of San Pedro. Close enough to use the marina without living with its noise or its parking.
Is San Pedro a real town or a resort?
A real town. It has a high street, a weekly market, schools, health centres and a resident population that stays through the winter -- which is not true of every address in Marbella. That is the main reason buyers choose it over the Golden Mile.
What is the difference between San Pedro and Guadalmina?
San Pedro is the town: walkable, level, busy. Guadalmina is immediately west, lower density and organised around the golf course, with larger plots and less foot traffic. Prices in Guadalmina are generally higher for the same built area.
Are the international schools nearby?
Yes. Several of the Costa del Sol’s international schools sit in and around San Pedro and Guadalmina, which is a large part of why the area holds its year-round population. We can confirm distances for a specific development.

From most of San Pedro, yes -- the boulevard runs from the town centre down to the promenade. From the Guadalmina golf-side addresses it is a short drive. We confirm the actual walking distance for a development rather than relying on a brochure claim.

Enquiry details may be processed in Nueva Living's customer relationship management system and shared with developers, legal advisers or other service providers only where necessary for a requested enquiry, viewing, reservation or service step. Website measurement events may be processed by Nueva Living's CRM and hosting providers for analytics and technical operation.
### The Chat Assistant
Soléa, the chat on this website, is an AI assistant. What you type is sent to Anthropic, which provides the AI model and processes the conversation on our behalf only to produce the answer; it does not use it to train its models. Anthropic may process it outside the European Union, under safeguards approved for such transfers. The conversation is kept in your browser until you close the tab. We keep an anonymous record of the questions asked and the searches made, without names, e-mail addresses or telephone numbers, to learn what buyers look for and what the website does not yet answer. Please do not enter sensitive information. If you ask to be contacted, the assistant sends your name and e-mail, and your phone number and message if you give them, to a Nueva Living advisor only after you agree, and we then handle them like any other enquiry. The answers are generated automatically from what this website publishes and can contain mistakes; an advisor confirms prices and availability.
### Nueva Living in ChatGPT and Claude
Nueva Living can be added to ChatGPT and to Claude as an app or connector. When you search through it, the assistant sends us only the criteria it passes on, such as area, budget, property type and any wishes you describe. It does not send your name or the rest of your conversation, and we do not record who searched. We do not keep a record of the searches. If you ask to be contacted, the assistant sends your name and e-mail, and your phone number and message if you give them, to a Nueva Living advisor only after you agree, and we then handle them like any other enquiry. OpenAI and Anthropic process the rest of your conversation under their own privacy policies.
### Introductions From Someone Else
If someone introduces you to Nueva Living through our referral page, we receive your name and contact details from them rather than from you. We rely on our legitimate interest in responding to that introduction, we tell you who gave us your details the first time we make contact, and you can ask us to stop there or at any point afterwards. Introduced details are not used for anything beyond that first conversation unless you choose to continue it.
### Retention & Rights
Enquiry details are kept for 24 months after our last contact with you and are then deleted. If you become a client, your details are kept for as long as the client relationship lasts and afterwards for the periods Spanish law requires. You may ask for access, correction or deletion at any time by writing to contact@nuevaliving.com, and you may complain to the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD).
